This is a Fully Remote Job

About Our Client:

The organization operates within the life sciences and healthcare industries, focusing on clinical research services, commercial insights, and healthcare intelligence. It addresses challenges in developing and commercializing innovative medical treatments aimed at improving patient outcomes and population health across the globe.

About the Opportunity:

The SENIOR PROJECT MANAGER leads a portfolio of client programs for non-profit, medical society, and patient advocacy organizations. This role is responsible for delivering multiple concurrent projects, managing financial performance, and maintaining executive-level client relationships. The position ensures predictable, well-governed delivery across complex, multi-workstream initiatives and plays a key role in driving operational discipline and client satisfaction.

Responsibilities:

Lead delivery across multiple concurrent programs including scope, schedule, budget, dependencies, and resourcing.
Consolidate project details into integrated program status, risk, decision, and financial reports.
Optimize capacity and manage tradeoffs and escalations.
Coordinate engineering, data, analytics, QA, and third-party partners to meet release milestones.
Serve as primary contact for client sponsors and senior stakeholders; lead governance and executive reviews.
Communicate complex issues into clear, decision-ready reports tailored to audiences.
Establish and maintain consistent delivery cadence with reporting and documentation.
Track commitments and action items to closure.
Assess risks and implement mitigation plans proactively.
Identify root causes of recurring issues and improve processes.
Manage program budgets, forecasts, utilization, margin, revenue recognition, and invoicing.
Manage scope changes and change orders.
Develop client relationships and identify opportunities for service expansion.
Coach and mentor project managers and delivery staff.
Promote accountability, preparation, and ownership within the team.

Requirements:

7+ years of project or program management experience with at least 3 years leading multi-project programs or portfolios with full financial accountability.
Experience managing executive-level client relationships in professional services, SaaS, or consulting.
Strong written and verbal communication skills; capable of leading senior-level meetings.
Familiarity with reporting cadences, governance structures, and delivery tracking tools (e.g., Jira, MS Project, Smartsheet).
Experience managing budgets, forecasts, and change control for multi-million dollar engagements.
Sound judgment and decisiveness under pressure.
Bachelor's degree in relevant field; PMP, PgMP, or equivalent certification preferred.
Preferred: experience with healthcare data, clinical registries, EHR integrations, HL7 FHIR standards.
Preferred: experience with Agile/SAFe or hybrid delivery involving multiple development partners.
Preferred: experience working with non-profit, medical society, or association clients.

Pay Range and Compensation Package:

The potential base pay range for this role, when annualized, is $88,100.00 - $220,200.00. Actual base pay may vary based on qualifications, location, and schedule. Additional incentive plans, bonuses, and benefits may be offered.

jobs.description:
Overview

GovCIO is currently hiring for Scrum Master/Project Manager to facilitating Agile processes, coordinating project activities, and providing operational support across the Product Line (PL). This role works closely with the Product Line Manager, Product Managers, teams, and stakeholders to ensure priorities are effectively managed, activities and deliverables are completed on schedule, and work remains aligned with organizational and customer objectives. This role is a fully remote position within the United States with core hours of operation from Monday to Friday, 8 AM to 5 PM ET.

Responsibilities

This role works closely with the Product Line Manager, Product Managers, teams, and stakeholders to ensure priorities are effectively managed, activities and deliverables are completed on schedule, and work remains aligned with organizational and customer objectives.

Partner with Product Leadership to coordinate initiatives, facilitate discussions, manage action items, and drive projects and operational priorities to successful completion.
Coordinate across multidisciplinary teams to align priorities, requirements, schedules, dependencies, resources, and deliverables while maintaining stakeholder engagement.
Facilitate Agile ceremonies, including Sprint Planning, Daily Stand-ups, Sprint Reviews, Retrospectives, and PI Planning, ensuring alignment with portfolio and product priorities.
Manage and maintain Jira, Jira Align, project plans, schedules, dashboards, and documentation to ensure accurate tracking of work, milestones, dependencies, and performance metrics.
Monitor project health by tracking progress, risks, issues, decisions, dependencies, and key performance indicators; facilitate resolution and escalation as needed.
Support backlog management by coordinating capacity planning, workload balancing, and refinement of user stories, tasks, and acceptance criteria.
Lead end-to-end data call operations across VA and GovCIO stakeholders by managing requirements, timelines, data governance, reporting, risk tracking, and executive communications using Jira and SharePoint.
Develop executive-ready communications, status reports, presentations, leadership briefings, and data-call responses by translating complex technical and business information into clear, actionable insights.
Continuously improve project management, reporting, and delivery processes while providing flexible, proactive support across evolving organizational priorities and mission objectives.

Qualifications

Required Skills and Experience

Bachelor's with 5 years (or commensurate experience)
Demonstrated experience as a Scrum Master, Project Manager, or in a comparable Agile delivery role.
Strong working knowledge of Agile methodologies, Scrum practices, and project management principles.
Hands-on experience facilitating Scrum events, Sprint planning, backlog management, and capacity planning.
Experience using Jira for work management, tracking, and reporting.
Experience coordinating projects, schedules, deliverables, milestones, and competing priorities.
Ability to work independently, anticipate needs, take initiative, and drive assignments to completion.
Strong organizational, analytical, problem-solving, and time-management skills.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including developing executive-level presentations and reports.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly PowerPoint, Excel, and Word.

Preferred Skills And Experience

Experience with Jira and enterprise-level Agile planning and reporting.
Experience supporting PI Planning and cross-team coordination.
Experience supporting complex IT programs or product lines, preferably within a federal government or VA environment.
Scrum Master certification (CSM, PSM, or equivalent) and/or Project Management Professional (PMP) certification.
Experience with Microsoft Teams and SharePoint.

Clearance Required:
Ability to obtain and maintain a Suitability/Public Trust clearance

Posted Salary Range: USD $90,000.00 - USD $95,000.00 /Yr.

jobs.description:
PROJECT MANAGER I

WHAT IS THE OPPORTUNITY?

The role of the Project Manager is to plan, execute, and finalize Bank projects according to timelines, milestone events and within budget. This includes acquiring resources, capacity planning and coordinating and motivating all project team members, contractors and or consultants to flawlessly complete project deliverables. Project Managers help define project objectives, scope and requirements; and ensure high levels of development and project execution throughout its life cycle. City National Bank Project Managers must adhere to the CNB Project Management Lifecycle Methodology.

Assembles project team, assigns individual responsibilities, identifies appropriate resources needed, and develops schedule to ensure timely completion of project and meeting deadlines of project.
Participates in meeting activities to identify project goals and gain consensus on project steps, schedule and implementation procedures; fosters cooperation and involvement of support team.
Interviews colleagues/client to identify and analyze needs; develops project plan and provides input to recommendations for request/problem resolution.
Identifies internal and/or external resources to ensure successful project completion.

Manages several projects of varying size concurrently and consults with all levels of management which may require coordinating activities across multiple departments and/or divisions.

Fosters and maintains good relationships with colleagues/clients to ensure that processes are integrated to support expected customer service levels. Acts as business partner by managing expectations and providing guidance and advice throughout project duration.

jobs.title: Senior Project Manager
jobs.description:
Who We Are

At Corebridge Financial, we believe action is everything. That’s why every day we partner with financial professionals and institutions to make it possible for more people to take action in their financial lives, for today and tomorrow.

We Align To a Set Of Values That Are The Core Pillars That Define Our Culture And Help Bring Our Brand Purpose To Life

We are stronger as one: We collaborate across the enterprise, scale what works and act decisively for our customers and partners.
We deliver on commitments: We are accountable, empower each other and go above and beyond for our stakeholders.
We learn, improve and innovate: We get better each day by challenging the status quo and equipping ourselves for the future.
We are inclusive: We embrace different perspectives, enabling our colleagues to make an impact and bring their whole selves to work.

Who You'll Work With

Institutional Markets (IM)
is the division within Corebridge Financial that manages funded and unfunded business with institutional clients. The Global Assumed Reinsurance business is a core part of IM and partners with institutional clients to deliver risk-transfer solutions across life insurance, annuity and pension products. The business combines disciplined underwriting, structuring expertise, balance-sheet strength and global asset sourcing to generate attractive risk-adjusted spread earnings. Asset-intensive reinsurance is a central focus of the growth strategy in Asia.

About The Role

We are seeking a highly organized, proactive professional to support the Head of Sales, Asia in building and executing the Global Assumed Reinsurance business in Japan and other Asian markets. Reporting directly to the Head of Sales, Asia, this role will serve as the central coordinator for regional client coverage, pipeline management, internal alignment and day-to-day business operations.

Business support includes preparing client and intermediary materials, maintaining market intelligence and tracking opportunities. Project management covers coordinating workstreams across product, actuarial, investments, legal, compliance and risk. Administrative and logistics duties include managing calendars, client meetings, regional business travel and events.

The successful candidate will help ensure that client engagement in Asia is well prepared, well documented and consistently followed up.The ideal candidate brings strong organizational and project management skills, sound business judgment, cross-cultural awareness and a genuine interest in insurance and reinsurance. The role requires excellent attention to detail, discretion in handling confidential information and the flexibility to support a fast-paced, globally distributed business across multiple time zones.

Responsibilities

Business Development Support: Support the Head of Sales, Asia in relationship development and opportunity origination with Japanese and other Asian life insurers, brokers, banks and other intermediaries. Prepare client briefing materials, meeting agendas, presentations and talking points.
Pipeline and CRM Management: Maintain an accurate, up-to-date pipeline of client relationships, prospects and opportunities. Track meeting outcomes, action items and next steps, and prepare regular pipeline reports for the Head of Sales, Asia and senior leadership.
Project Management: Coordinate cross-functional workstreams for priority opportunities and strategic initiatives. Manage timelines, deliverables, dependencies and status reporting across product, actuarial, investments, structuring, finance, legal, compliance, tax and risk.
Market Research and Intelligence: Gather, organize and analyze information on client strategies, competitive activity, regulatory and accounting developments, and market conditions in Japan and other Asian markets. Summarize key insights in concise briefing notes.
Internal Reporting and Governance Support: Prepare materials for internal management meetings, steering committees and governance forums. Coordinate input from internal partners and track follow-up actions to completion.
NDA and Documentation Coordination: Coordinate the preparation, review and tracking of NDAs, term sheets and other documentation with Legal and Compliance. Maintain organized records of client communications and documents.
Calendar and Meeting Management: Manage scheduling and logistics for client meetings, internal meetings and conference calls across multiple time zones. Finalize and distribute meeting materials, and prepare meeting notes and follow-up communications.
Travel and Logistics Management: Plan and coordinate business travel to Japan and other Asian markets, including itineraries, air and ground transportation, hotels, meeting venues, client dinners and social events. Support expense reporting and budget tracking.
Events and Client Engagement: Coordinate participation in industry conferences, client events, roadshows and delegation visits, including logistics, attendee management, materials and post-event follow-up.
Administrative Support: Provide day-to-day administrative support to the Head of Sales, Asia and the regional team, including correspondence, document management, vendor coordination and onboarding support for new team members.
Collaboration: Build strong working relationships with internal stakeholders, executive assistants, IT, Facilities and partner teams across Corebridge Financial to ensure smooth execution of regional activities.

Skills And Qualifications

5 + years of relevant experience in insurance, reinsurance, asset management, investment banking or institutional financial services, including business development, project management or client coverage support.
Proven project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities, meet deadlines and drive cross-functional deliverables to completion.
Strong organizational, time management and analytical skills, with excellent attention to detail.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English, including the ability to prepare clear, concise materials for senior leaders and external clients.
Understanding of the Japanese language and business culture is a plus.
Strong interest in Japan and the broader Asia region, with a genuine passion for cross-cultural exchange and international business.
Experience coordinating travel, meetings and events for senior executives, ideally involving international counterparts.
High degree of discretion and professionalism in handling confidential and sensitive information.
Highly proficient in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams and SharePoint). Experience with CRM tools is a plus.
Willingness to work flexible hours across multiple time zones, including early-morning and evening calls with Japan and other Asian markets, and to travel to the region as business needs require.
Bachelor’s degree in business, finance, economics or a related field required.
Highly organized and dependable, with a strong sense of ownership and follow-through.
Client-focused and service-oriented, with polished, professional communication.
Intellectually curious and eager to build expertise in reinsurance and institutional markets.
Culturally aware and effective at working with colleagues and counterparts across geographies and seniority levels.
Proactive, assertive and highly responsive, taking initiative, anticipating needs, reacting quickly to requests, and confidently voicing ideas, concerns and recommendations in a constructive and respectful manner.
Collaborative team player who builds trust and works effectively across functions.
Agile and adaptable, comfortable managing shifting priorities in a fast-paced environment.

Compensation

The anticipated salary range for this position is at the commencement of employment. Not all candidates will be eligible for the upper end of the salary range. The actual compensation offered will ultimately be dependent on multiple factors, which may include the candidate’s geographic location, skills, experience and other qualifications.

In addition, the position is eligible for a discretionary bonus in accordance with the terms of the applicable incentive plan.

This position is based in Corebridge Financial’s Jersey City, NJ and Woodland Hills, CA. office and is subject to our hybrid working policy, which gives colleagues the benefits of working both in an office and remotely.

Why Corebridge?

At Corebridge Financial, we prioritize the health, well-being, and work-life balance of our employees. Our comprehensive benefits and wellness program is designed to support employees both personally and professionally, ensuring that they have the resources and flexibility needed to thrive.

jobs.title: Senior Project Manager
jobs.description:
The Sr. Project Manager serves as the primary on-site point of contact and liaison between the internal project team, clients, installers, and construction partners. This role is responsible for the successful planning, coordination, and execution of furniture installations from initial site verification through final client walk-through. Key responsibilities include managing installation schedules, labor quoting and budgets, shipping and delivery coordination, change orders, and overall installation quality and performance. The Sr. Project Manager verifies site conditions, resolves product and installation issues in the field, coordinates with general contractors and subcontractors, and attends construction meetings as required.

This position maintains consistent communication with internal teams, lead installers, and clients; tracks billable project management time; supports the development of junior project managers through coaching and mentoring; assists with departmental training initiatives; and performs other related duties as assigned to support business operations.

Requirements

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

None

KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES

Installation Planning & Execution

Plan, coordinate, and oversee all aspects of furniture installation, including schedule, labor, quality, budget, and overall execution.
Create and manage installation schedules aligned with construction milestones and client move-in dates.
Monitor shipping, delivery, and installation activities to ensure timely and accurate execution.
Track installation progress from start to completion and proactively address issues or delays.
Request, review, and manage labor quotes from third-party installation vendors.
Manage and track change orders related to labor and project scope.

Site & Field Coordination

Verify site conditions, including field measurements, existing product inventory, paths of travel, power, and data locations.
Resolve product or installation issues efficiently and professionally in the field.
Coordinate closely with general contractors, subcontractors, and installers to maintain project schedules.
Attend construction and coordination meetings as required.

Communication & Collaboration

Maintain consistent, clear communication with internal project teams, lead installers, and clients throughout the installation process.
Serve as a reliable on-site representative of KBM Hogue during installation activities.

Leadership & Departmental Support

Support and develop junior project managers through coaching and mentoring.
Assist Project Management leadership with departmental training initiatives and process improvements.
Assist with the curation of Standards Binders when requested.

Administrative & Time Tracking

Regularly track and report billable project management time.
Perform other related duties as assigned by management.

QUALIFICATIONS

Education & Experience

Bachelor’s degree (BS or BA) from a four-year college or university, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Minimum of 8 years of experience in furniture project management or a related field (e.g., construction management).
Strong ability to learn and utilize business operating systems.
Experience with MS Project and PlanGrid preferred.
Excellent time management and prioritization skills; ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously.
Highly motivated with strong problem-solving and decision-making abilities.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Demonstrates a strong spirit of teamwork and collaboration.
Willingness to work evenings, weekends, and occasional holidays as required.
Prolonged periods of sitting and working on a computer.
Ability to lift up to 25 pounds as needed.
Reliable transportation required.
Travel: Approximately 20–30%, including travel to KBM Hogue offices in Northern California, client sites, and occasional overnight domestic travel.
Work Schedule: Hybrid, minimum of three (3) on-site days per week

Who You'll Work With

Institutional Markets (IM)
is the division within Corebridge Financial that manages funded and unfunded business with institutional clients. The Global Assumed Reinsurance business is a core part of IM and partners with institutional clients to deliver risk-transfer solutions across life insurance, annuity and pension products. The business combines disciplined underwriting, structuring expertise, balance-sheet strength and global asset sourcing to generate attractive risk-adjusted spread earnings. Asset-intensive reinsurance is a central focus of the growth strategy in Asia.

About The Role

We are seeking a highly organized, proactive professional to support the Head of Sales, Asia in building and executing the Global Assumed Reinsurance business in Japan and other Asian markets. Reporting directly to the Head of Sales, Asia, this role will serve as the central coordinator for regional client coverage, pipeline management, internal alignment and day-to-day business operations.

Business support includes preparing client and intermediary materials, maintaining market intelligence and tracking opportunities. Project management covers coordinating workstreams across product, actuarial, investments, legal, compliance and risk. Administrative and logistics duties include managing calendars, client meetings, regional business travel and events.

The successful candidate will help ensure that client engagement in Asia is well prepared, well documented and consistently followed up.The ideal candidate brings strong organizational and project management skills, sound business judgment, cross-cultural awareness and a genuine interest in insurance and reinsurance. The role requires excellent attention to detail, discretion in handling confidential information and the flexibility to support a fast-paced, globally distributed business across multiple time zones.

Responsibilities

Business Development Support: Support the Head of Sales, Asia in relationship development and opportunity origination with Japanese and other Asian life insurers, brokers, banks and other intermediaries. Prepare client briefing materials, meeting agendas, presentations and talking points.
Pipeline and CRM Management: Maintain an accurate, up-to-date pipeline of client relationships, prospects and opportunities. Track meeting outcomes, action items and next steps, and prepare regular pipeline reports for the Head of Sales, Asia and senior leadership.
Project Management: Coordinate cross-functional workstreams for priority opportunities and strategic initiatives. Manage timelines, deliverables, dependencies and status reporting across product, actuarial, investments, structuring, finance, legal, compliance, tax and risk.
Market Research and Intelligence: Gather, organize and analyze information on client strategies, competitive activity, regulatory and accounting developments, and market conditions in Japan and other Asian markets. Summarize key insights in concise briefing notes.
Internal Reporting and Governance Support: Prepare materials for internal management meetings, steering committees and governance forums. Coordinate input from internal partners and track follow-up actions to completion.
NDA and Documentation Coordination: Coordinate the preparation, review and tracking of NDAs, term sheets and other documentation with Legal and Compliance. Maintain organized records of client communications and documents.
Calendar and Meeting Management: Manage scheduling and logistics for client meetings, internal meetings and conference calls across multiple time zones. Finalize and distribute meeting materials, and prepare meeting notes and follow-up communications.
Travel and Logistics Management: Plan and coordinate business travel to Japan and other Asian markets, including itineraries, air and ground transportation, hotels, meeting venues, client dinners and social events. Support expense reporting and budget tracking.
Events and Client Engagement: Coordinate participation in industry conferences, client events, roadshows and delegation visits, including logistics, attendee management, materials and post-event follow-up.
Administrative Support: Provide day-to-day administrative support to the Head of Sales, Asia and the regional team, including correspondence, document management, vendor coordination and onboarding support for new team members.
Collaboration: Build strong working relationships with internal stakeholders, executive assistants, IT, Facilities and partner teams across Corebridge Financial to ensure smooth execution of regional activities.

Skills And Qualifications

5 + years of relevant experience in insurance, reinsurance, asset management, investment banking or institutional financial services, including business development, project management or client coverage support.
Proven project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities, meet deadlines and drive cross-functional deliverables to completion.
Strong organizational, time management and analytical skills, with excellent attention to detail.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English, including the ability to prepare clear, concise materials for senior leaders and external clients.

Strong interest in Japan and the broader Asia region, with a genuine passion for cross-cultural exchange and international business.
Experience coordinating travel, meetings and events for senior executives, ideally involving international counterparts.
High degree of discretion and professionalism in handling confidential and sensitive information.
Highly proficient in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams and SharePoint). Experience with CRM tools is a plus.
Willingness to work flexible hours across multiple time zones, including early-morning and evening calls with Japan and other Asian markets, and to travel to the region as business needs require.
Bachelor’s degree in business, finance, economics or a related field required.
Highly organized and dependable, with a strong sense of ownership and follow-through.
Client-focused and service-oriented, with polished, professional communication.
Intellectually curious and eager to build expertise in reinsurance and institutional markets.
Culturally aware and effective at working with colleagues and counterparts across geographies and seniority levels.
Proactive, assertive and highly responsive, taking initiative, anticipating needs, reacting quickly to requests, and confidently voicing ideas, concerns and recommendations in a constructive and respectful manner.

jobs.description:
Minimum qualifications:

Bachelor's degree in a technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
8 years of experience in program management.
Experience managing the end-to-end hardware NPI lifecycle (from concept through EVT/DVT/PVT validation to volume manufacturing and deployment) for data center physical infrastructure, such as high-density AI/server rack systems, liquid cooling and thermal management (e.g., CDUs, manifolds, cold plates), or rack/row power distribution and energy storage systems.

Preferred qualifications:

Master's degree or PhD in Mechanical, Electrical, Thermal, or Systems Engineering, or equivalent hardware experience.
Experience leading hyperscale data center physical infrastructure programs across mechanical racks (e.g., ORv3, seismic/structural), liquid cooling (CDUs, heat exchangers, manifolds, cold plates), or high-density AC/high-voltage DC power and battery/capacitive backup.
Understanding of hyperscale and colocation facility interfaces, AI accelerator thermal/power envelopes, CapEx/NRE business cases, and executive leadership.
Track record managing JDM/ODM/OEM partners through EVT/DVT/PVT builds, DFM/DFA qualification, compliance, and global production ramps.

About The Job

A problem isn’t truly solved until it’s solved for all. That’s why Googlers build products that help create opportunities for everyone, whether down the street or across the globe. As a Technical Program Manager at Google, you’ll use your technical expertise to lead complex, multi-disciplinary projects from start to finish. You’ll work with stakeholders to plan requirements, identify risks, manage project schedules, and communicate clearly with cross-functional partners across the company. You're equally comfortable explaining your team's analyses and recommendations to executives as you are discussing the technical tradeoffs in product development with engineers.

As a Senior Technical Program Manager, you will lead the end-to-end hardware New Product Introduction (NPI) lifecycle from initial concept architecture and system co-design through EVT/DVT/PVT validation, pilot builds, and high-volume deployment across both Google-owned hyperscale data centers and strategic cloud expansion sites worldwide.

Operating at the intersection of silicon, server systems, and data center facilities, you will drive flagship hardware programs across our core physical infrastructure pillars next-generation high-density AI/ML and compute rack architectures, megawatt-scale liquid cooling and thermal management systems (e.g., Coolant Distribution Units [CDUs], heat exchangers, rack/row manifolds, and cold-plate loops), and high-capacity rack and row power delivery and energy storage (AC and high-voltage DC power shelves, DC busways, Battery Backup Units [BBUs], and AI transient load-smoothing systems). You will partner directly with Principal and Distinguished Engineers, Silicon and System Architects, Data Center Engineering and Operations, Global Supply Chain, and tier-1 ODM/OEM manufacturers to turn industry-first physical infrastructure designs into deployed AI capacity at global scale.

The AI and Infrastructure team is redefining what’s possible. We empower Google customers with breakthrough capabilities and insights by delivering AI and Infrastructure at unparalleled scale, efficiency, reliability and velocity. Our customers include Googlers, Google Cloud customers, and billions of Google users worldwide.

We're the driving force behind Google's groundbreaking innovations, empowering the development of our cutting-edge AI models, delivering unparalleled computing power to global services, and providing the essential platforms that enable developers to build the future. From software to hardware our teams are shaping the future of world-leading hyperscale computing, with key teams working on the development of our TPUs, Vertex AI for Google Cloud, Google Global Networking, Data Center operations, systems research, and much more.

Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

US: $192000 - $278000 (USD) + 20% bonus target + equity + benefits

Responsibilities

Learn more about benefits at Google .

Lead phase-gate hardware New Product Introduction (NPI) execution (Concept through EVT/DVT/PVT, pilot, and production ramp) for high-density AI/compute rack enclosures, megawatt-scale liquid cooling and thermal systems (CDUs, manifolds, cold plates), or rack/row power distribution and energy storage.
Drive system co-design, intercept schedules, and facility interface alignment between physical infrastructure and AI/ML payload teams (TPU, GPU, Compute, Networking) across both Google-owned hyperscale data centers and third-party colocation expansion sites.
Partner with Global Supply Chain, Supplier Quality Engineering, and ODM/JDM/OEM manufacturers to manage tooling, DFM/DFA qualification, regulatory compliance, and volume ramps while resolving critical-path engineering trade-offs, CapEx/NRE budgets, and executive readiness reviews.

jobs.title: Senior, Technical Program Manager
jobs.description:
About Compal
Compal is a global leader in electronics design and manufacturing. Our Austin-area facility builds high-performance AI servers for leading technology customers, combining advanced manufacturing, rigorous quality systems and fast, flexible execution. We are growing our team and looking for people who thrive in a fast-paced, customer-driven environment.

Position Summary
The Technical Program Manager (TPM) owns the engineering relationship with assigned customers. The TPM captures the customer's technical requirements and drives them through Compal's internal engineering functions, including manufacturing engineering, test engineering, quality engineering, process engineering and IT/MES, as well as through external suppliers delivering technical and automation solutions. The TPM makes sure every requirement is understood, assigned, carried out, validated and closed, so that products are built and tested to customer specifications on schedule. The ideal candidate combines a strong engineering background with program management discipline and the communication skills to work credibly with customer engineering teams.

Key Responsibilities

Serve as the primary technical point of contact for assigned customers, building strong working relationships with customer engineering, quality and operations teams.

Capture, clarify and document customer technical requirements, including product specifications, build and configuration requirements, test and validation requirements, quality standards, data and traceability requirements, and packaging.

Translate customer requirements into clear engineering deliverables, assign owners across manufacturing, test, quality and process engineering, and drive them to on-time completion.

Maintain a requirements traceability matrix and track every requirement from intake through implementation, validation and customer sign-off.

Lead technical reviews with customers and internal teams, such as design for manufacturing and test (DFM/DFT) reviews, process and test readiness reviews, first article inspections (FAI) and build readiness reviews.

Manage engineering changes (ECOs/ECNs) from the customer: assess technical, schedule and cost impact; coordinate implementation; and confirm correct cut-in on the production line.

Drive new product introduction (NPI) programs from early engineering builds (EVT/DVT/PVT) through the transition to volume production.

Manage suppliers delivering technical and automation solutions (such as test systems, fixtures, automation equipment and software), including requirements definition, statements of work, schedules, factory and site acceptance testing (FAT/SAT), and handover.

Partner with quality and test engineering on technical issues, failure analysis, yield improvement and corrective actions (8D/CAPA), and communicate root cause and status to the customer.

Identify technical risks and gaps early, develop mitigation plans, and escalate with clear options and recommendations.

Report program status, technical KPIs (yield, first-pass yield, test coverage, open issues, change status) and milestone progress to customers and leadership.

Capture lessons learned and drive improvements in engineering processes, requirements handling and program execution.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Electrical, Mechanical, Industrial, Computer or Manufacturing Engineering, or a related technical field.

At least 5 years of experience as a technical program manager, engineering program manager or equivalent role in a manufacturing environment, preferably electronics, EMS/ODM, server or data center hardware.

Strong technical understanding of electronics manufacturing processes (SMT, system assembly and rack integration), test strategies (ICT, functional and system-level test), and quality engineering methods.

Proven experience managing customer technical requirements and driving them through cross-functional engineering teams.

Experience managing suppliers or vendors of technical solutions, equipment or automation.

Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to discuss technical details with engineers and summarize clearly for leadership and customers.

Ability to lead cross-functional teams without direct authority and to manage several programs and priorities at once.

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with working knowledge of structured methods such as 8D, root cause analysis and FMEA.

Proficiency with Microsoft Office and project management tools, and working knowledge of ERP/MES systems.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with AI servers, GPU-based systems, high-performance computing, liquid cooling or rack-level integration.

Experience working directly with engineering teams at tier-one technology or hyperscale customers.

Experience with factory automation, test automation or manufacturing software and data systems.

Familiarity with IPC standards, ISO 9001 quality systems, and Lean or Six Sigma methods.

PMP, Lean or Six Sigma certification.

Bilingual English / Mandarin Chinese is a plus.

Key Competencies

Technical depth and sound engineering judgment

Customer focus and credibility with engineering teams

Structured, disciplined requirements and change management

Clear, proactive communication

Collaboration and influence across functions and suppliers

Our Austin-area facility builds high-performance AI servers for leading technology customers, combining advanced manufacturing, rigorous quality systems and fast, flexible execution. We are growing our team and looking for people who thrive in a fast-paced, customer-driven environment.

Position Summary
The Manufacturing Program Manager owns the day-to-day execution of customer requirements for assigned AI server programs. Acting as the primary link between the customer and our internal teams, this role ensures that build plans, quality expectations, engineering changes and delivery commitments are clearly understood, translated into actionable plans, and executed on time. The ideal candidate combines strong communication skills with a solid understanding of business and manufacturing processes, and is comfortable driving cross-functional teams to results.

Key Responsibilities

Serve as the primary day-to-day point of contact for assigned customers, managing communication, expectations and escalations.

Translate customer requirements (specifications, build instructions, forecasts, quality and test requirements) into clear, actionable plans for production, test, quality, materials and engineering teams.

Drive daily execution against build plans and delivery commitments; monitor output, yield, WIP and shipment status and resolve issues that put commitments at risk.

Lead regular customer and internal program reviews, including daily/weekly status meetings, KPI reporting and quarterly business reviews.

Manage engineering change orders (ECOs/ECNs), new revisions and configuration changes, ensuring timely implementation across documentation, materials and the production floor.

Coordinate with planning and supply chain on forecasts, material readiness, shortages and clear-to-build status.

Partner with quality and test engineering on customer complaints, failure analysis, RMAs and corrective actions (8D/CAPA), and track actions to closure.

Support new product introduction (NPI) and transitions to volume production, including pilot builds, readiness reviews and lessons learned.

Identify program risks early, develop mitigation plans and escalate appropriately with clear options and recommendations.

Track program financials and business metrics such as revenue, cost, inventory exposure and on-time delivery; support quotes and pricing inputs as needed.

Maintain accurate program documentation, schedules and records in ERP/MES and program management tools.

Drive continuous improvement in program processes, customer satisfaction and operational performance.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Business, Supply Chain, Operations Management or a related field, or equivalent experience.

At least 5 years of experience as a program manager, project manager or equivalent role in a manufacturing environment, preferably electronics, EMS/ODM, server or data center hardware.

Solid understanding of business and manufacturing processes, including production planning, materials management, quality systems, test and change management.

Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to present clearly to customers and to all levels of the organization.

Proven ability to lead cross-functional teams without direct authority and to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with a data-driven approach to decisions.

Proficiency with Microsoft Office (Excel, PowerPoint, Project) and working knowledge of ERP/MES systems (e.g., SAP, Oracle).

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with AI servers, high-performance computing, rack-level integration or data center infrastructure products.

Experience working with tier-one technology or hyperscale customers.

Familiarity with IPC standards, ISO 9001 quality systems and lean manufacturing / Six Sigma methods.

PMP, Lean or Six Sigma certification.

Bilingual English / Mandarin Chinese is a plus.

Key Competencies

Customer focus and ownership of results

Clear, proactive and professional communication

Execution discipline and attention to detail

Business acumen and sound judgment

Collaboration and influence across functions

This position is based on-site at our Austin-area manufacturing facility and combines office work with regular time on the production floor. jobs.title: Senior, NPI Program Manager
jobs.description:
About Compal
Compal is a global leader in electronics design and manufacturing. Our Austin-area facility builds high-performance AI servers for leading technology customers, combining advanced manufacturing, rigorous quality systems and fast, flexible execution. We are growing our team and looking for people who thrive in a fast-paced, customer-driven environment.

Position Summary
The NPI Program Manager leads the introduction of new AI server products and product transfers into manufacturing at our Austin-area facility. Working closely with customer and internal engineering design organizations, the NPI PM drives each new design from early development through the product development life cycle (EVT, DVT and PVT) to a stable, high-yield volume launch. The role owns the NPI schedule and readiness across process development, design for manufacturing (DFM), supply chain qualification, test development and quality, making sure every product is ready to build at quality, cost and volume. The ideal candidate combines strong program management discipline with hands-on knowledge of electronics manufacturing and the product development process.

Key Responsibilities

Lead NPI programs and product transfers from kickoff to volume production, owning the integrated schedule, milestones, deliverables and readiness gates.

Serve as the main link between design engineering organizations (customer and internal) and the Austin manufacturing site, making sure designs are manufacturable, testable and supportable.

Plan and run EVT, DVT and PVT builds: define build plans, quantities and configurations; coordinate material, process, test and quality readiness; and lead post-build reviews and exit criteria.

Drive design for manufacturing, test and assembly (DFM/DFT/DFA) reviews, capture feedback and track design changes to closure with the design teams.

Lead product transfers from other Compal sites, customer sites or design centers, including transfer plans, documentation, equipment and fixture moves, process replication and validation, and knowledge transfer.

Drive process development with manufacturing, process and industrial engineering, including assembly processes, work instructions, line layout, fixtures, tooling, cycle time and capacity planning.

Coordinate test development with test engineering, including test strategy, test coverage, fixtures and stations, and test software readiness.

Lead supply chain qualification with procurement, supplier quality and planning: new parts and suppliers, first article inspections (FAI), PPAP or equivalent, lead times, and material readiness for each build.

Own the bill of materials (BOM) and engineering change readiness for NPI builds, making sure BOMs, revisions and ECOs are correct in ERP/MES before each build.

Track and drive NPI quality and readiness metrics such as first-pass yield, defect trends, open issues, DFM actions and readiness checklists, and lead root cause and corrective action for build issues.

Run phase-gate and production readiness reviews, and lead the formal handoff from NPI to sustaining manufacturing and program management.

Identify schedule, technical and supply risks early, develop mitigation plans, and escalate with clear options and recommendations.

Report NPI status, risks and milestones to customers, design teams and leadership, and support NPI cost tracking and quotes as needed.

Capture lessons learned and continuously improve the NPI process, templates and checklists.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Electrical, Mechanical, Industrial, Manufacturing or Computer Engineering, or a related technical field.

At least 5 years of experience in NPI program management, NPI engineering or an equivalent role in electronics manufacturing, preferably EMS/ODM, server or data center hardware.

Hands-on experience leading products through the product development life cycle (EVT, DVT, PVT) and into volume production.

Experience with product transfers between sites or from design centers into manufacturing.

Strong knowledge of electronics manufacturing processes (SMT, PCBA, system assembly and rack integration), DFM/DFT principles, and test strategies.

Working knowledge of supply chain and supplier qualification, including BOM management, FAI and new part qualification.

Excellent communication skills, with the ability to work credibly with design engineers, manufacturing teams, suppliers, customers and leadership.

Proven ability to lead cross-functional teams without direct authority and manage several programs at once in a fast-paced environment.

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with working knowledge of structured methods such as 8D, root cause analysis and PFMEA.

Proficiency with Microsoft Office and project management tools, and working knowledge of ERP/MES and PLM systems.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with AI servers, GPU-based systems, high-performance computing, liquid cooling or rack-level integration.

Experience working with tier-one technology or hyperscale customers and their design teams.

Experience with phase-gate product development processes and production readiness assessments.

Familiarity with IPC standards, ISO 9001 quality systems, and Lean or Six Sigma methods.

PMP, Lean or Six Sigma certification.

Bilingual English / Mandarin Chinese is a plus.

Key Competencies

Ownership of schedules, readiness and launch results

Technical understanding of design and manufacturing

Structured planning and phase-gate discipline

Clear, proactive communication

Collaboration and influence across design, manufacturing and supply chain

Role: Data Analyst / Analytics Engineer

About the Company
A high-growth fintech platform is scaling two core data initiatives: a credit bureau intelligence engine that turns financial signals into automated underwriting logic, and an embedded health membership product distributed across its large lending base. This role sits at the intersection of credit data, user behavior, and multi-channel campaign analytics to power real-time eligibility engines, customer targeting models, and product-mapping triggers.

Role Overview
A hands-on, build-from-scratch position focused on turning raw data into working scripts, decision rules, and evaluation models without reliance on pre-built dashboards.

Credit Bureau Data Analysis: Work with raw bureau files (scores, tradeline histories, account classifications, enquiry velocity) to build risk segmentations, scoring rules, and lending eligibility logic.

Signal-to-Trigger Mapping: Build algorithmic triggers linking credit behavior changes to contextual health and financial protection offerings.
Pipelines & Experimentation: Develop repeatable Python and SQL workflows for A/B testing, cohort tracking, and executive performance reviews.
Data Hygiene & Structuring: Ingest, clean, and standardize large-scale CRM files, call logs, and bureau extracts for cross-functional product and growth teams.

Candidate Profile

Experience: 0–2 years in Data Analytics, Data Science, or a related analytical discipline (internships included).
Technical Stack: Strong proficiency in Python (pandas, numpy) and SQL, alongside spreadsheet modeling for rapid analysis.
Analytical Skills: Solid grasp of statistics, cohort dynamics, and performance metrics (precision, approval bands, conversion rates).
Domain Curiosity: High interest in credit bureau data, digital lending, and fintech/insurtech intersections.
Execution: Comfort with unstructured, messy datasets and the ability to articulate technical insights to business stakeholders.
Nice-to-Haves: Exposure to classification models, lightweight internal dashboards (HTML/JS), or lending/insurance underwriting logic.

Description

Looking for an opportunity to make an impact?

At Leidos, we deliver innovative solutions through the efforts of our diverse and talented people who are dedicated to our customers’ success. We empower our teams, contribute to our communities, and operate sustainable. Everything we do is built on a commitment to do the right thing for our customers, our people, and our community. Our Mission, Vision, and Values guide the way we do business.

If this sounds like a mission you want to be a part of, keep reading!

Leidos is seeking an experienced DoWIN Operations Analyst to support the Defense Manpower Data Center (DMDC) CyberPRIMES program. Leidos is a major partner on the contract and will provide a substantial portion of the cybersecurity workforce supporting the Personnel Readiness Management Agency (PRMA) and DMDC.

The DoDIN Operations Analyst will maintain cyber operational situational awareness, coordinate cybersecurity activities across enterprise stakeholders, track cyber taskings and remediation efforts, support incident response coordination, and prepare operational reporting for leadership. This position serves as the operational bridge between the Security Operations Center (SOC), Cyber Defense teams, Network Operations, System Owners, Risk Management Framework (RMF) stakeholders, and leadership to ensure timely execution of cybersecurity actions and mission requirements across the DMDC enterprise.

Work Locations:

Mark Center, Alexandria, Virginia – 1 position

Mission Environment

DMDC supports the Personnel Readiness Management Agency (PRMA) within the Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Personnel and Readiness (OUSD(P&R)) and maintains the Department of Defense’s largest and most comprehensive central repository of personnel, manpower, casualty, pay, entitlement, personnel security, identity, readiness, training, and related data.

The PRMA Information Technology (IT) environment includes approximately 15,000 network and endpoint devices supporting more than 600 Government-Off-The-Shelf (GOTS) applications and approximately 100 Risk Management Framework (RMF) authorization boundaries managed through the Enterprise Mission Assurance Support Service (eMASS). The DoDIN Operations Analyst operates within the DMDC Cyber Operations environment and supports continuous monitoring, operational coordination, cyber situational awareness, vulnerability management, incident management, and mission assurance activities. The position provides operational oversight and coordination across cybersecurity stakeholders to support the security, availability, and resilience of DMDC systems, networks, and mission-critical services.

Primary Tasks

Maintain situational awareness of cybersecurity activity, emerging threats, vulnerabilities, incidents, and operational impacts affecting DMDC systems, applications, and networks.
Review DoD, Intelligence Community, CISA, vendor, and open-source reporting to identify vulnerabilities, malware, threat activity, and risks relevant to the DMDC environment.
Analyze cybersecurity operational information to identify trends, recurring issues, operational risks, and potential mission impacts.
Develop and disseminate situational awareness reports, threat notifications, operational summaries, and executive-level status updates.
Serve as a coordination point for cybersecurity activities involving SOC analysts, incident responders, cybersecurity engineers, network operations personnel, RMF teams, and system owners.
Track cybersecurity taskings, incident-response actions, vulnerability-remediation efforts, compliance requirements, and other operational activities through completion.
Coordinate implementation, validation, mitigation, and reporting of cybersecurity actions across multiple stakeholders.
Support cyber incident management activities by tracking incidents, coordinating stakeholder communications, and ensuring appropriate escalation procedures are followed.
Monitor vulnerability remediation activities and support validation of corrective actions across systems and authorization boundaries.
Assist with management and tracking of Plans of Action and Milestones (POA&Ms), cybersecurity findings, and compliance activities.
Prepare executive-level briefings, dashboards, reports, and decision-support products for leadership.
Translate technical cybersecurity information into operational impacts, risk assessments, and recommended courses of action for technical and non-technical audiences.
Coordinate stakeholder communications during significant cybersecurity events, operational disruptions, and incident-response activities.
Support cybersecurity assessments, inspections, audits, and reporting requirements.
Contribute to process improvements, operational procedures, reporting workflows, and coordination activities to enhance mission effectiveness.
Maintain complete and accurate records of cybersecurity operational activities, task status, risk information, and supporting documentation in Government-approved systems.

Basic Qualifications

BS degree or equivalent and 2-6 years of prior relevant experience, or a Master's degree with less experience, in cybersecurity operations, network operations, cyber defense, information assurance, or related fields.
Experience supporting cybersecurity operations, cyber defense, incident management, vulnerability management, or continuous monitoring activities.
Experience coordinating activities among multiple technical and operational stakeholders.
Experience developing operational reports, executive briefings, dashboards, or cybersecurity status updates.
Experience tracking cybersecurity taskings, remediation efforts, corrective actions, or compliance activities.
Working knowledge of cybersecurity operations, Computer Network Defense (CND), incident-response processes, and threat management principles.
Understanding of TCP/IP networking, enterprise network architectures, cybersecurity controls, and defense-in-depth concepts.
Ability to analyze operational information and assess cybersecurity risk and mission impact.
Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to brief technical and non-technical audiences.
Ability to work effectively within a team-based cybersecurity operations environment.
U.S. Citizenship required.
Active Secret security clearance required.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience supporting Department of Defense cyber operations, DoWIN Operations, Security Operations Centers (SOC), Network Operations Centers (NOC), or Cybersecurity Service Provider (CSSP) environments.
Experience supporting DMDC, PRMA, DISA, or other large DoD enterprise environments.
Experience briefing senior leaders, Senior Executive Service (SES) personnel, General Officers, or Flag Officers.
Experience with Risk Management Framework (RMF), eMASS, Continuous Monitoring, and cybersecurity compliance requirements.
Experience managing Plans of Action and Milestones (POA&Ms), cybersecurity findings, and remediation activities.
Experience with Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) platforms, vulnerability management tools, and enterprise cybersecurity monitoring solutions.
Experience supporting cybersecurity incident response, vulnerability management, mission assurance, or operational reporting activities.
Familiarity with Department of Defense cybersecurity policies, requirements, and operational procedures.
Experience operating within a 24x7 mission environment supporting critical enterprise services

jobs.title: Executive – Data Analyst (Ops Strategy)
jobs.description:
About The Role

We are looking for a Data Analyst Executive to sit at the centre of how operations performs and

what it costs. From last-mile delivery and warehousing to fleet and vendor management, you will

build the reporting and analysis that tells us what is working, what is slipping, and where money

is leaking.

This is not a passive reporting role. You will own recurring dashboards, dig into performance

and cost deviations, and build the analysis that supports network, vendor, and process

decisions.

Key Responsibilities

Operational Performance Analytics

Own daily and weekly dashboards across delivery performance, TAT/SLA adherence,

cancellations, and warehouse throughput.

Investigate deviations — late dispatches, failed tasks, out-of-stock incidents, vehicle

idling — and identify root causes.

Track productivity and utilisation across manpower, fleet, and warehouse capacity.

Cost & Unit Economics

Track cost per delivery, cost per trip, cost per item handled, and city-level cost-to-serve.
Maintain month-on-month cost dashboards by city, cost head, and vendor with clear

variance commentary.

Reconcile PO vs. GRN vs. invoice; audit vendor billing against rate cards and escalate

deviations.

Identify cost leakages — idle capacity, empty return trips, excess deployment — and

size the savings.

Ops Strategy & Projects

Build business cases for network and vendor decisions: in-house vs. 3PL, fleet mix,

warehouse footprint, route restructuring.

Support demand and capacity planning with volume trends and forecasting inputs.
Run what-if analysis before rollout and measure impact after; support pilots and process

improvement projects end to end.

Automation & Reporting Hygiene

Automate recurring MIS using scripting or scheduled queries.
Use AI tools (ChatGPT, Claude, and similar) to speed up script writing, query building,

and data cleaning — with validation owned by you, not the tool.

Maintain metric definitions and data quality checks so numbers stay consistent across

teams.

Stakeholder Management

Partner with city ops, fleet, warehouse, procurement, and finance to align on definitions,

targets, and cut-offs.

Present reviews to leadership in a decision-ready format — insight first, method second.

Must-Have Skills

Advanced Excel / Google Sheets — can build a reporting workbook or cost model from

scratch.

SQL — joins, aggregations, window functions, CTEs; comfortable with large

transactional tables.

Analytical reasoning — can decompose a number into its drivers and explain what

actually moved.

AI tools for analytics — uses ChatGPT, Claude, or similar to accelerate analysis, and

validates every output before it reaches a report.

Business sense — connects a metric to the operational decision behind it.
Ownership and detail — reconciles before publishing; treats an unexplained variance

as their problem to close.

Good-to-Have Skills

Google Apps Script (or equivalent) for report automation and trigger-based workflows.
MongoDB aggregation pipelines and Metabase or a similar query/dashboard layer.
Exposure to procurement / P2P flows — PO, GRN, invoicing, cost heads.
Prior experience in logistics, e-commerce, supply chain, or rental/subscription

operations.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Statistics, Mathematics, Economics, Commerce, or a

related quantitative field.

0–3 years in data analytics, MIS, business analysis, or operations strategy.
Freshers with strong SQL and spreadsheet skills are encouraged to apply.

Why Join Us

Direct line of sight into how operational decisions get made; your analysis reaches

decision-makers the same week.

Autonomy to build the reporting stack from first principles.
Steep learning curve across supply chain, fleet, warehousing, procurement, and

commercial negotiation.

jobs.description:
Who We Are

At Corebridge Financial, we believe action is everything. That’s why every day we partner with financial professionals and institutions to make it possible for more people to take action in their financial lives, for today and tomorrow.

We Align To a Set Of Values That Are The Core Pillars That Define Our Culture And Help Bring Our Brand Purpose To Life

We are stronger as one: We collaborate across the enterprise, scale what works and act decisively for our customers and partners.
We deliver on commitments: We are accountable, empower each other and go above and beyond for our stakeholders.
We learn, improve and innovate: We get better each day by challenging the status quo and equipping ourselves for the future.
We are inclusive: We embrace different perspectives, enabling our colleagues to make an impact and bring their whole selves to work.

Who You’ll Work With

Institutional Markets (IM)
is the division within Corebridge Financial that manages funded and unfunded business with institutional clients. The Global Assumed Reinsurance business is a core part of IM and partners with institutional clients to deliver risk-transfer solutions across life insurance, annuity and pension products. The business combines disciplined underwriting, structuring expertise, balance-sheet strength and global asset sourcing to generate attractive risk-adjusted spread earnings. Asset-intensive reinsurance is a central focus of the growth strategy in Asia.

About The Role

We are seeking a detail-oriented, analytical and highly organized Business Analyst to support the Head of Sales, Asia and the regional Global Assumed Reinsurance team .
R

eporting to the Head of Sales, Asia and working closely with the Associate Project Manager, this role will deliver business analysis and reporting, support client and internal meeting preparation, and manage the day-to-day administration and logistics that keep the regional business running smoothly.

The ideal candidate is proactive and agile, enjoys working with data and information, and is comfortable supporting a fast-paced, globally distributed team across multiple time zones. This is an excellent opportunity for an early-career professional to build expertise in reinsurance and institutional markets while gaining exposure to senior leaders and clients in Japan and other Asian markets.

Responsibilities

Data and Reporting: Gather, organize and analyze business data to identify trends, patterns and areas for improvement. Prepare regular reports and dashboards on client activity, pipeline status and regional business performance.
Pipeline and Client Information Support: Maintain client, intermediary and opportunity records in the CRM and tracking tools, ensuring information is accurate, complete and up to date.
Strategic Initiatives: Collaborate with the Associate Project Manager and the broader team on regional strategic initiatives, and track progress, action items and deadlines through status reporting.
Market Research: Conduct research on Japanese and other Asian life insurers, competitors, industry trends and regulatory developments. Prepare concise summaries and background materials for the Head of Sales, Asia.
Meeting Preparation: Support client meetings, internal meetings and management reviews in a proactive, agile manner based on priorities. Prepare presentations, briefing books, agendas and meeting notes, and track follow-up actions.
Calendar Management: Manage calendar logistics and meeting scheduling across multiple time zones, including finalizing and distributing meeting materials.
Travel Management: Manage travel arrangements for the Head of Sales, Asia and team members, including air and ground transportation, hotels, client dinners, social events and expense reports.
Events and Visitor Support: Support logistics for industry conferences, client events and visiting delegations, including venue arrangements, attendee lists, materials and follow-up.
In-Office Management: Provide administrative support for day-to-day operations, including correspondence, document filing, supplies, printing, invoice processing and vendor coordination.
Collaboration: Establish strong relationships throughout the organization and partner with executive assistants, IT Executive Support, Facilities and other team members.
Organizational Agility: Navigate the organization effectively by learning and mastering internal systems, protocols and culture.

Skills And Qualifications

2 plus years of professional experience in the financial services or insurance industry required
Proven experience in business analysis and/or administrative support, preferably at an executive level.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to turn data into clear, actionable insights.
Solid organizational and time management skills, with keen attention to detail.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.
Understanding of the Japanese language and business culture is a plus.
Strong interest in Japan and the broader Asia region, with a genuine passion for cross-cultural exchange and international business.
Basic understanding of, or willingness to learn about, life insurance, annuities and reinsurance; prior exposure to institutional markets is a plus.
High degree of discretion and professionalism in handling confidential information.
Highly proficient in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams, SharePoint and Visio).
Willingness to work flexible hours across multiple time zones, including early-morning and evening calls with Japan and other Asian markets, and to travel occasionally as business needs require.
Bachelor’s degree in business administration, finance, economics or a related field required.
Analytical and intellectually curious, eager to grow in a global business.
Highly organized and dependable, with strong follow-through.
Service-oriented and agile, adapting smoothly to shifting priorities in a fast-paced environment.
Culturally aware and comfortable working with colleagues and counterparts across geographies.
Proactive, assertive and highly responsive, taking initiative, anticipating needs, reacting quickly to requests, and confidently voicing ideas, concerns and recommendations in a constructive and respectful manner.
Collaborative team player who contributes to a culture of teamwork, innovation and inclusion.

Compensation

The anticipated salary range for this position is $70,000 - $100,000 base salary at the commencement of employment. Not all candidates will be eligible for the upper end of the salary range. The actual compensation offered will ultimately be dependent on multiple factors, which may include the candidate’s geographic location, skills, experience and other qualifications.

In addition, the position is eligible for a discretionary bonus in accordance with the terms of the applicable incentive plan.

Work Location

This position is based in Corebridge Financial’s Jersey City, NJ or Woodland Hills, CA. office and is subject to our hybrid working policy, which gives colleagues the benefits of working both in an office and remotely.

Why Corebridge?

At Corebridge Financial, we prioritize the health, well-being, and work-life balance of our employees. Our comprehensive benefits and wellness program is designed to support employees both personally and professionally, ensuring that they have the resources and flexibility needed to thrive.

Benefit Offerings Include

Health and Wellness: We offer a range of medical, dental and vision insurance plans, as well as mental health support and wellness initiatives to promote overall well-being.
Retirement Savings: We offer retirement benefits options, which vary by location. In the U.S., our competitive 401(k) Plan offers a generous dollar-for-dollar Company matching contribution of up to 6% of eligible pay and a Company contribution equal to 3% of eligible pay (subject to annual IRS limits and Plan terms). These Company contributions vest immediately.
Employee Assistance Program: Confidential counseling services and resources are available to all employees.
Matching charitable donations: Corebridge matches donations to tax-exempt organizations 1:1, up to $5,000.
Volunteer Time Off: Employees may use up to 16 volunteer hours annually to support activities that enhance and serve communities where employees live and work.
Paid Time Off: Eligible employees start off with at least 24 Paid Time Off (PTO) days so they can take time off for themselves and their families when they need it.

Eligibility for and participation in employer-sponsored benefit plans and Company programs will be subject to applicable law, governing Plan document(s) and Company policy.
