new_jobs.description:
Minimum qualifications:

Bachelor's degree in a technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
8 years of experience in program management.
Experience managing the end-to-end hardware NPI lifecycle (from concept through EVT/DVT/PVT validation to volume manufacturing and deployment) for data center physical infrastructure, such as high-density AI/server rack systems, liquid cooling and thermal management (e.g., CDUs, manifolds, cold plates), or rack/row power distribution and energy storage systems.

Preferred qualifications:

Master's degree or PhD in Mechanical, Electrical, Thermal, or Systems Engineering, or equivalent hardware experience.
Experience leading hyperscale data center physical infrastructure programs across mechanical racks (e.g., ORv3, seismic/structural), liquid cooling (CDUs, heat exchangers, manifolds, cold plates), or high-density AC/high-voltage DC power and battery/capacitive backup.
Understanding of hyperscale and colocation facility interfaces, AI accelerator thermal/power envelopes, CapEx/NRE business cases, and executive leadership.
Track record managing JDM/ODM/OEM partners through EVT/DVT/PVT builds, DFM/DFA qualification, compliance, and global production ramps.

About The Job

A problem isn’t truly solved until it’s solved for all. That’s why Googlers build products that help create opportunities for everyone, whether down the street or across the globe. As a Technical Program Manager at Google, you’ll use your technical expertise to lead complex, multi-disciplinary projects from start to finish. You’ll work with stakeholders to plan requirements, identify risks, manage project schedules, and communicate clearly with cross-functional partners across the company. You're equally comfortable explaining your team's analyses and recommendations to executives as you are discussing the technical tradeoffs in product development with engineers.

As a Senior Technical Program Manager, you will lead the end-to-end hardware New Product Introduction (NPI) lifecycle from initial concept architecture and system co-design through EVT/DVT/PVT validation, pilot builds, and high-volume deployment across both Google-owned hyperscale data centers and strategic cloud expansion sites worldwide.

Operating at the intersection of silicon, server systems, and data center facilities, you will drive flagship hardware programs across our core physical infrastructure pillars next-generation high-density AI/ML and compute rack architectures, megawatt-scale liquid cooling and thermal management systems (e.g., Coolant Distribution Units [CDUs], heat exchangers, rack/row manifolds, and cold-plate loops), and high-capacity rack and row power delivery and energy storage (AC and high-voltage DC power shelves, DC busways, Battery Backup Units [BBUs], and AI transient load-smoothing systems). You will partner directly with Principal and Distinguished Engineers, Silicon and System Architects, Data Center Engineering and Operations, Global Supply Chain, and tier-1 ODM/OEM manufacturers to turn industry-first physical infrastructure designs into deployed AI capacity at global scale.

The AI and Infrastructure team is redefining what’s possible. We empower Google customers with breakthrough capabilities and insights by delivering AI and Infrastructure at unparalleled scale, efficiency, reliability and velocity. Our customers include Googlers, Google Cloud customers, and billions of Google users worldwide.

We're the driving force behind Google's groundbreaking innovations, empowering the development of our cutting-edge AI models, delivering unparalleled computing power to global services, and providing the essential platforms that enable developers to build the future. From software to hardware our teams are shaping the future of world-leading hyperscale computing, with key teams working on the development of our TPUs, Vertex AI for Google Cloud, Google Global Networking, Data Center operations, systems research, and much more.

Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

US: $192000 - $278000 (USD) + 20% bonus target + equity + benefits

Responsibilities

Learn more about benefits at Google .

Lead phase-gate hardware New Product Introduction (NPI) execution (Concept through EVT/DVT/PVT, pilot, and production ramp) for high-density AI/compute rack enclosures, megawatt-scale liquid cooling and thermal systems (CDUs, manifolds, cold plates), or rack/row power distribution and energy storage.
Drive system co-design, intercept schedules, and facility interface alignment between physical infrastructure and AI/ML payload teams (TPU, GPU, Compute, Networking) across both Google-owned hyperscale data centers and third-party colocation expansion sites.
Partner with Global Supply Chain, Supplier Quality Engineering, and ODM/JDM/OEM manufacturers to manage tooling, DFM/DFA qualification, regulatory compliance, and volume ramps while resolving critical-path engineering trade-offs, CapEx/NRE budgets, and executive readiness reviews.

new_jobs.title: Senior, Technical Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
About Compal
Compal is a global leader in electronics design and manufacturing. Our Austin-area facility builds high-performance AI servers for leading technology customers, combining advanced manufacturing, rigorous quality systems and fast, flexible execution. We are growing our team and looking for people who thrive in a fast-paced, customer-driven environment.

Position Summary
The Technical Program Manager (TPM) owns the engineering relationship with assigned customers. The TPM captures the customer's technical requirements and drives them through Compal's internal engineering functions, including manufacturing engineering, test engineering, quality engineering, process engineering and IT/MES, as well as through external suppliers delivering technical and automation solutions. The TPM makes sure every requirement is understood, assigned, carried out, validated and closed, so that products are built and tested to customer specifications on schedule. The ideal candidate combines a strong engineering background with program management discipline and the communication skills to work credibly with customer engineering teams.

Key Responsibilities

Serve as the primary technical point of contact for assigned customers, building strong working relationships with customer engineering, quality and operations teams.

Capture, clarify and document customer technical requirements, including product specifications, build and configuration requirements, test and validation requirements, quality standards, data and traceability requirements, and packaging.

Translate customer requirements into clear engineering deliverables, assign owners across manufacturing, test, quality and process engineering, and drive them to on-time completion.

Maintain a requirements traceability matrix and track every requirement from intake through implementation, validation and customer sign-off.

Lead technical reviews with customers and internal teams, such as design for manufacturing and test (DFM/DFT) reviews, process and test readiness reviews, first article inspections (FAI) and build readiness reviews.

Manage engineering changes (ECOs/ECNs) from the customer: assess technical, schedule and cost impact; coordinate implementation; and confirm correct cut-in on the production line.

Drive new product introduction (NPI) programs from early engineering builds (EVT/DVT/PVT) through the transition to volume production.

Manage suppliers delivering technical and automation solutions (such as test systems, fixtures, automation equipment and software), including requirements definition, statements of work, schedules, factory and site acceptance testing (FAT/SAT), and handover.

Partner with quality and test engineering on technical issues, failure analysis, yield improvement and corrective actions (8D/CAPA), and communicate root cause and status to the customer.

Identify technical risks and gaps early, develop mitigation plans, and escalate with clear options and recommendations.

Report program status, technical KPIs (yield, first-pass yield, test coverage, open issues, change status) and milestone progress to customers and leadership.

Capture lessons learned and drive improvements in engineering processes, requirements handling and program execution.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Electrical, Mechanical, Industrial, Computer or Manufacturing Engineering, or a related technical field.

At least 5 years of experience as a technical program manager, engineering program manager or equivalent role in a manufacturing environment, preferably electronics, EMS/ODM, server or data center hardware.

Strong technical understanding of electronics manufacturing processes (SMT, system assembly and rack integration), test strategies (ICT, functional and system-level test), and quality engineering methods.

Proven experience managing customer technical requirements and driving them through cross-functional engineering teams.

Experience managing suppliers or vendors of technical solutions, equipment or automation.

Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to discuss technical details with engineers and summarize clearly for leadership and customers.

Ability to lead cross-functional teams without direct authority and to manage several programs and priorities at once.

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with working knowledge of structured methods such as 8D, root cause analysis and FMEA.

Proficiency with Microsoft Office and project management tools, and working knowledge of ERP/MES systems.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with AI servers, GPU-based systems, high-performance computing, liquid cooling or rack-level integration.

Experience working directly with engineering teams at tier-one technology or hyperscale customers.

Experience with factory automation, test automation or manufacturing software and data systems.

Familiarity with IPC standards, ISO 9001 quality systems, and Lean or Six Sigma methods.

PMP, Lean or Six Sigma certification.

Bilingual English / Mandarin Chinese is a plus.

Key Competencies

Technical depth and sound engineering judgment

Customer focus and credibility with engineering teams

Structured, disciplined requirements and change management

Clear, proactive communication

Collaboration and influence across functions and suppliers

Description

Looking for an opportunity to make an impact?

At Leidos, we deliver innovative solutions through the efforts of our diverse and talented people who are dedicated to our customers’ success. We empower our teams, contribute to our communities, and operate sustainable. Everything we do is built on a commitment to do the right thing for our customers, our people, and our community. Our Mission, Vision, and Values guide the way we do business.

If this sounds like a mission you want to be a part of, keep reading!

Leidos is seeking an experienced DoWIN Operations Analyst to support the Defense Manpower Data Center (DMDC) CyberPRIMES program. Leidos is a major partner on the contract and will provide a substantial portion of the cybersecurity workforce supporting the Personnel Readiness Management Agency (PRMA) and DMDC.

The DoDIN Operations Analyst will maintain cyber operational situational awareness, coordinate cybersecurity activities across enterprise stakeholders, track cyber taskings and remediation efforts, support incident response coordination, and prepare operational reporting for leadership. This position serves as the operational bridge between the Security Operations Center (SOC), Cyber Defense teams, Network Operations, System Owners, Risk Management Framework (RMF) stakeholders, and leadership to ensure timely execution of cybersecurity actions and mission requirements across the DMDC enterprise.

Work Locations:

Mark Center, Alexandria, Virginia – 1 position

Mission Environment

DMDC supports the Personnel Readiness Management Agency (PRMA) within the Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Personnel and Readiness (OUSD(P&R)) and maintains the Department of Defense’s largest and most comprehensive central repository of personnel, manpower, casualty, pay, entitlement, personnel security, identity, readiness, training, and related data.

The PRMA Information Technology (IT) environment includes approximately 15,000 network and endpoint devices supporting more than 600 Government-Off-The-Shelf (GOTS) applications and approximately 100 Risk Management Framework (RMF) authorization boundaries managed through the Enterprise Mission Assurance Support Service (eMASS). The DoDIN Operations Analyst operates within the DMDC Cyber Operations environment and supports continuous monitoring, operational coordination, cyber situational awareness, vulnerability management, incident management, and mission assurance activities. The position provides operational oversight and coordination across cybersecurity stakeholders to support the security, availability, and resilience of DMDC systems, networks, and mission-critical services.

Primary Tasks

Maintain situational awareness of cybersecurity activity, emerging threats, vulnerabilities, incidents, and operational impacts affecting DMDC systems, applications, and networks.
Review DoD, Intelligence Community, CISA, vendor, and open-source reporting to identify vulnerabilities, malware, threat activity, and risks relevant to the DMDC environment.
Analyze cybersecurity operational information to identify trends, recurring issues, operational risks, and potential mission impacts.
Develop and disseminate situational awareness reports, threat notifications, operational summaries, and executive-level status updates.
Serve as a coordination point for cybersecurity activities involving SOC analysts, incident responders, cybersecurity engineers, network operations personnel, RMF teams, and system owners.
Track cybersecurity taskings, incident-response actions, vulnerability-remediation efforts, compliance requirements, and other operational activities through completion.
Coordinate implementation, validation, mitigation, and reporting of cybersecurity actions across multiple stakeholders.
Support cyber incident management activities by tracking incidents, coordinating stakeholder communications, and ensuring appropriate escalation procedures are followed.
Monitor vulnerability remediation activities and support validation of corrective actions across systems and authorization boundaries.
Assist with management and tracking of Plans of Action and Milestones (POA&Ms), cybersecurity findings, and compliance activities.

About The Role

We are looking for a Data Analyst Executive to sit at the centre of how operations performs and

what it costs. From last-mile delivery and warehousing to fleet and vendor management, you will

build the reporting and analysis that tells us what is working, what is slipping, and where money

is leaking.

This is not a passive reporting role. You will own recurring dashboards, dig into performance

and cost deviations, and build the analysis that supports network, vendor, and process

decisions.

Key Responsibilities

Operational Performance Analytics

Own daily and weekly dashboards across delivery performance, TAT/SLA adherence,

cancellations, and warehouse throughput.

Investigate deviations — late dispatches, failed tasks, out-of-stock incidents, vehicle

idling — and identify root causes.

Track productivity and utilisation across manpower, fleet, and warehouse capacity.

Cost & Unit Economics

Track cost per delivery, cost per trip, cost per item handled, and city-level cost-to-serve.
Maintain month-on-month cost dashboards by city, cost head, and vendor with clear

variance commentary.

Reconcile PO vs. GRN vs. invoice; audit vendor billing against rate cards and escalate

deviations.

Identify cost leakages — idle capacity, empty return trips, excess deployment — and

size the savings.

Ops Strategy & Projects

Build business cases for network and vendor decisions: in-house vs. 3PL, fleet mix,

warehouse footprint, route restructuring.

Support demand and capacity planning with volume trends and forecasting inputs.
Run what-if analysis before rollout and measure impact after; support pilots and process

improvement projects end to end.

Automation & Reporting Hygiene

Automate recurring MIS using scripting or scheduled queries.
Use AI tools (ChatGPT, Claude, and similar) to speed up script writing, query building,

and data cleaning — with validation owned by you, not the tool.

Maintain metric definitions and data quality checks so numbers stay consistent across

teams.

Stakeholder Management

Partner with city ops, fleet, warehouse, procurement, and finance to align on definitions,

targets, and cut-offs.

Present reviews to leadership in a decision-ready format — insight first, method second.

Must-Have Skills

Advanced Excel / Google Sheets — can build a reporting workbook or cost model from

scratch.

SQL — joins, aggregations, window functions, CTEs; comfortable with large

transactional tables.

Analytical reasoning — can decompose a number into its drivers and explain what

actually moved.

AI tools for analytics — uses ChatGPT, Claude, or similar to accelerate analysis, and

validates every output before it reaches a report.

Business sense — connects a metric to the operational decision behind it.
Ownership and detail — reconciles before publishing; treats an unexplained variance

as their problem to close.

Good-to-Have Skills

Google Apps Script (or equivalent) for report automation and trigger-based workflows.
MongoDB aggregation pipelines and Metabase or a similar query/dashboard layer.
Exposure to procurement / P2P flows — PO, GRN, invoicing, cost heads.
Prior experience in logistics, e-commerce, supply chain, or rental/subscription

operations.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Statistics, Mathematics, Economics, Commerce, or a

related quantitative field.

0–3 years in data analytics, MIS, business analysis, or operations strategy.
Freshers with strong SQL and spreadsheet skills are encouraged to apply.

Why Join Us

Direct line of sight into how operational decisions get made; your analysis reaches

decision-makers the same week.

Autonomy to build the reporting stack from first principles.
Steep learning curve across supply chain, fleet, warehousing, procurement, and

commercial negotiation.

eporting to the Head of Sales, Asia and working closely with the Associate Project Manager, this role will deliver business analysis and reporting, support client and internal meeting preparation, and manage the day-to-day administration and logistics that keep the regional business running smoothly.

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to turn data into clear, actionable insights.

eporting to the Head of Sales, Asia and working closely with the Associate Project Manager, this role will deliver business analysis and reporting, support client and internal meeting preparation, and manage the day-to-day administration and logistics that keep the regional business running smoothly.

new_jobs.title: GTM Data Analyst
new_jobs.description:
MarginEdge is hiring an Analyst
to build out go-to-market analytics: pipeline and conversion reporting, coverage and capacity modeling, commission calculation, and the analysis leadership uses to decide where to put money and headcount.

The enticing part of this role is that you own the whole path. You'll help frame the question, write the SQL, build the model, put it in source control, and present the answer — and the version you build is the one the company keeps using. There's no analytics team you hand a spec to. That's the trade: you have to be technical enough to build it, and you get to skip the six weeks of translation.

You'll report to the Director of Data Platform and Analytics and sit inside the data team, with Revenue Operations as your primary stakeholder. Your work gets reviewed by people who care whether the model is sound, and your roadmap comes from what the revenue organization actually needs. You'll work regularly with the Director of Revenue Operations, the CRO, and FP&A — more direct exposure to how revenue decisions get made than this kind of role usually carries.

We care much more about how you think and what you can build than where you've worked. Consulting, finance, RevOps, a BI seat at a smaller company, a science or engineering background you've since pointed at data problems — all fine.

MarginEdge: Where hospitality meets technology

As a team built by former (and current!) restaurant operators, our mission is to bring operators the same energy, attention to detail, and passion that they bring to their guests. Our culture is deeply rooted in service, partially because that’s where so many of our team come from (including everyone on our Business Development team), but also because we believe it is just the right way to run a business. We design our software with profound empathy for the complexity of running a restaurant, and the goal of making the magic just a little easier for operators by taking the complex (read: very annoying) back office tasks off their plate, while empowering them with real-time data.

Our founders share a deep history in both owning and operating restaurants and in building successful tech companies. We are venture-backed and serve 12,000+ restaurants across the US and Canada.

We enable restaurants to make magic while knowing we are doing the same for them.

We have the utmost respect for our clients and because of this, we are unable to hire their current employees.

What type of responsibilities will I have?

Build the analysis that decides things.

Build the analysis behind weekly pipeline reviews, forecast reviews, monthly business reviews, and sales board reporting, and take over more of it as you ramp.
Own stage-to-stage conversion reporting: conversion rates, cycle times, and win rates by channel, team, segment, and product.
Build assumption-based models for strategic initiatives — new segments, pricing changes, channel bets — with the assumptions parameterized rather than buried in a formula.
Help run and extend the coverage and capacity models: work the revenue target back to the pipeline and headcount required, and flag the gap early enough that leadership can act on it.
Contribute to the pipeline-based bottoms-up forecast and its reconciliation against the sales team commitment and the top-down model.
Investigate the unglamorous questions — why a cohort converted worse than the one before it, why cycle time moved in one segment and not another — and bring them to leadership before you're asked.

Build the thing that answers them next quarter.

Build and maintain the GTM layer of our dbt project: funnel and conversion models, pipeline history, rep and territory attribution.
Ship through source control — branch, pull request, review, tests, documentation. Your code gets reviewed, and eventually you'll review other people's.
Reconcile Salesforce, subscription billing, and product usage data, and become the person who can explain precisely why they disagree when they do.
Help define GTM metrics in our semantic layer, with RevOps as the metric owner, so self-service and agent-based querying return governed numbers rather than someone's best guess.

Use AI as a real tool and check its work.

Use Claude for query drafting, model scaffolding, and analysis iteration, and help RevOps stakeholders get useful work out of it.
QA AI output seriously: know what the query actually did, catch the plausible-but-wrong answer, and be able to explain the mechanism behind a finding rather than repeating it.

What qualifications or skills are required?

Demonstrated professional experience doing analytical work where you were expected to structure some of the problem yourself, not just execute a spec.
Strong SQL. CTEs, joins, and window functions should be comfortable. More importantly, when a query returns a number that looks wrong, you find out why rather than running it again.
Working knowledge of source control — branches, commits, pull requests. You don't need to have worked on a large codebase, but if your instinct is to build in a shared spreadsheet, this role will frustrate you.
Enough curiosity about how data gets where it is to reason about where a number came from and when it last landed. You won't own ingestion.
Real spreadsheet skill. A lot of what you produce lands in Excel in front of an executive, and you should be able to build a multi-tab model someone else can follow and extend.
The ability to say the number is wrong to a room that would prefer it weren't, and an obsession with accuracy that survives deadline pressure.
Funnel and SaaS metrics: conversion rate, pipeline coverage, cycle time, gross and net retention, CAC, payback. If you already know what breaks each one, great. If not, you'll learn them here, and you should be able to explain them by month three.

Nice to Haves:

dbt — Core, project structure, tests, macros. If you've built tested, version-controlled transformation logic some other way, say so.
Trino/Athena or Snowflake. We're mid-migration, so you'd see both.
Python for the analysis SQL shouldn't do.
Salesforce as a data source, including the parts of it that lie to you.
Subscription billing data (Zuora or similar), quota setting, territory design, or sales compensation modeling.
Semantic or metrics layer experience (MetricFlow, Cube, or similar).
BI development in Preset/Superset, Looker, Tableau, or comparable.

Compensation:
The anticipated salary range for this role is $90,000–$110,000
annually. Where a candidate falls within that range depends on a variety of factors, including experience, skills, qualifications, geographic location, and internal equity. In addition to base salary, this role may be eligible for bonus opportunities and our comprehensive benefits package.

What’s it like to work for MarginEdge?

Imagine the fun of a great restaurant - surrounded by a team of people (including some that you help to manage!) who care about hospitality, care about quality, and care about each other - then subtract the long nights, weekends, drunk customers at the bar...et voila, MarginEdge!

We work hard, we work fast and we fuel our work with a commitment of transparency from leadership, straight talk and trust between teams. We believe that the best people do their best work when they feel empowered - so whether you are remote or in our office (likely eating a catered lunch from our clients in our baller, brand new penthouse HQ in Ballston) you get to work with your manager to call your shot on what works best for you. Did we mention it has a full commercial kitchen and is walking distance (covered walking, that is) from the metro?

Benefits (Shut The Front Door, They Are Amazing)

In order to fuel this rocket ship, we need to build a team as passionate about our work and product as we are. We believe that top talent (that’s you!) should feel deeply connected to their work, appreciated for the time they give to building our organization and have the balance necessary to give their best during work hours and all those after-hours too. We do this by offering a suite of kick ass benefits not only to be competitive and catch the eye of super smart people (that’s you again!) but also provide the foundation for a career you love and a life outside of work you love just as much.

Unlimited Paid Time Off (and we mean it, we encourage your healthy work life balance!)
Medical, Dental, Vision, and Short/Long-Term Disability Insurance (preventative care for the win)
Health Savings Account with employer match (dependent upon your medical plan selection)
Commuter benefits with employer contribution (excluding limos and helos - for now)
Generous Life Insurance Plan
Short- and Long-term Disability
Company-Paid Holidays
401(k) and matching
Stock Options to buy into everything we are doing to support this industry
12-week fully Paid Parental Leave
Lunch catered twice a week at our HQ in Arlington (we exclusively cater from our clients, too!
A wellness program that sponsors healthy activities such as step challenges and provides discounts to gyms and fitness classes.

Check out our 100% “Recommend to a Friend” rating from anonymous employee reviews on
Glassdoor
.

Oh, and our recognition in the Washington Post as a
top small businesses
to work for in 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025!

And most important, what our customers think about our work on
Capterra
and
G2 Crowd.

Our Fine Print is Bold:

We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran, marital, disability status or any other characteristic protected by law. new_jobs.description:
Research Analyst

Organisation: ALLSET

Location: Remote

Reporting to: Research Lead

Contract: 1-year contract (3 days/week) with a 3-month probation period

ALLSET is a climate preparedness research centre focused on how trust, moral values, and everyday life shape the way communities interpret, respond and recover from extreme weather events. Its focus is on applied research in climate-exacerbated disaster areas. The team has started projects in Northern Sumatra (Indonesia), Rio Grande do Sul (Brazil), El Salvador, Guatemala and Honduras (Central America), France and Greece (Southern Europe) and the Caribbean.

VISION A world where extreme weather events are well understood by the communities who experience them and people have agency over the solutions that address them

MISSION To conduct research focused on the lived experience of extreme weather events and draw upon these lessons to improve preparedness and adaptation efforts, as well as broader education and advocacy opportunities for climate change mitigation.

What We Aim To Do

ALLSET works with communities affected by extreme weather to understand how people experience disasters, navigate uncertainty and rebuild their lives. We examine how decisions are made under pressure, how local knowledge and trusted relationships shape responses, and how social, cultural and material conditions influence people's ability to prepare, cope and recover.

Our research follows human response across the disaster cycle, from anticipation and immediate action to long-term recovery and adaptation. Using ethically rigorous, trauma-informed and culturally grounded methods, we bring together place-based inquiry, cross-context comparison and longitudinal learning to understand how experiences and behaviours evolve over time.

ONE, ALLSET develops evidence on the human dimensions of extreme weather. We investigate how risk is understood, how people mobilise resources and support, and how formal systems are experienced in everyday life. This reveals the factors that enable or constrain individual and collective capacity, complementing technical and institutional assessments with insights grounded in lived reality.

TWO, we connect this evidence with the organisations and networks that shape disaster response, including public institutions, humanitarian organisations, researchers, civil society, funders and community leaders. Through these relationships, we translate research into insights that can inform policy, practice, investment and public engagement, helping decision-makers design responses that are more responsive to the realities of the people they serve.

Allset is seeking an experienced and driven Research Associate to conduct analysis of human-centered data in the context of extreme weather events.

The Research Associate will strengthen ALLSET’s analytical and research capacity, supporting the rigorous analysis, synthesis and communication of findings across multiple geographies. The role will work closely with the Research Lead to process and interpret large volumes of qualitative and quantitative data, ensuring consistency, methodological rigour and analytical depth across regions.

Research Analysis & Synthesis:
The Research Associate will lead and support the analysis and synthesis of incoming qualitative and quantitative data, working alongside the Research Lead to identify patterns, interpret findings and draw connections across contexts. This includes strengthening analytical consistency across regional datasets.

Content, Quality & Storytelling:
The role will support the review and quality assurance of regional reports and other research outputs, ensuring findings are accurately represented, analytically coherent and communicated clearly. It will also help translate complex research into compelling narratives suited to different audiences, including researchers, practitioners and decision-makers.

Academic & External Outputs: The Research Associate may contribute to the development of higher-level research outputs, including co-authored academic papers, working papers and other publications.

Key Responsibilities

Translate practitioner and organisational needs into clear, feasible, and ethically robust research questions and designs.
Oversee qualitative and quantitative analysis to generate clear, relevant, and actionable insights, in collaboration with Research Lead and Project Leads
Synthesise complex evidence into concise narratives tailored to technical and non-technical audiences.
Establish and continuously improve research processes, standards, and ethical protocols across projects

Profile we are looking for

6-8+ years of experience conducting applied social research
Strong grounding in both qualitative and quantitative research analysis, and interpretation.
Experience managing and working with external research agencies or partners for data collection.
Strong ethical awareness and a demonstrated commitment to responsible research practice.
Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain complex research clearly to diverse audiences.
Interest in new and emerging research methodologies and approaches.
Fluency in English
PhD or commensurate experience in a relevant field.

new_jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Cleared
new_jobs.description:
About Aalyria

Aalyria is a leading technology company that supplies laser communications technology and temporospatial software-defined networking platforms to the aerospace industry. With technology acquired from Google, Aalyria is at the forefront of innovation in satellite and airborne mesh networks, as well as cislunar and deep-space communications. We are revolutionizing the orchestration and management of planetary mesh networks using any radio or optical spectrum, any orbit, and any hardware across land, sea, air, and space.

Role Overview

Aalyria's Spacetime platform orchestrates highly dynamic aerospace networks using a temporospatial Software Defined Networking (SDN) approach, managing not just routing but the physical link topology and lower-layer configuration underneath it.

We're looking for a Technical Program Manager to own execution on one of our most sensitive customer programs, work that requires an active TS/SCI clearance

, with a polygraph strongly preferred given the access levels involved. You'll be the linchpin between Aalyria's engineering teams and a cleared government customer, driving technical tradeoffs directly rather than simply tracking them. Engineering will look to you to make sequencing, scope, and architecture-adjacent calls, and to represent program status and risk with complete accuracy to customer stakeholders who may not always have full visibility into every technical detail.

This is a role for someone who can operate independently inside a classified environment, hold their own in a room with Staff or Principal engineers, and get things done through influence rather than authority.

Key Responsibilities

End-to-End Technical Program Execution: Own program planning and execution for a classified Spacetime engineering effort, driving the work through each phase of the mission and directly resolving cross-system dependencies and technical tradeoffs, not just surfacing them for others to decide.
Cleared Customer & Stakeholder Leadership: Serve as the primary programmatic interface with a cleared government customer, communicating fluently with both technical staff and senior government stakeholders across classified and unclassified channels.
Cross-Functional Orchestration: Run the operating rhythm, such as kickoffs, technical reviews, exec readouts, that keeps Engineering, Product, and Solutions Engineering aligned on status, risk, and decisions across compartmented and uncompartmented workstreams.
Requirements Translation & Technical Judgment: Translate customer and mission requirements into actionable engineering plans. You should be able to read and critique a design document unaided, and reason in real time about latency, throughput, scaling, and failure-mode tradeoffs.
Security & Compliance Stewardship: Handle classified information and CUI correctly as a matter of course, maintain a sound personal security posture, and follow program security and export-control (ITAR/EAR) requirements without needing to be reminded. Partner closely with the FSO and IT/Cybersecurity, who are direct stakeholders in how this role is evaluated.
Contract & Financial Management: Own T&M or cost-type contract reporting requirements, including monthly labor, subcontract, hardware, and materials tracking at the Master Equipment List (MEL) level to support invoicing.
Risk & Delivery Coordination: Identify schedule, scope, and dependency risk early; escalate with context; and coordinate mitigations directly with engineering leads across development, staging, and dedicated government cloud production environments.

Required Qualifications

Active TS/SCI clearance in good standing. TS/SCI with polygraph is strongly preferred given the access levels this role requires.
5+ years of experience in technical program management, engineering program management, or a closely related role delivering complex technical platforms, ideally for U.S. Government or defense/space customers.
Demonstrated technical depth: the ability to read and critique a design document unaided, and to engage engineering teams on architecture, scaling, and failure-mode tradeoffs as a peer, not a translator.
A track record with genuinely technical programs, infrastructure migrations, API/interface contracts, cross-system dependency resolution, or multi-team technical rollouts, not just cross-functional coordination with a technical flavor.
Proven ability to influence without authority and interface confidently with senior government and customer stakeholders.
Experience managing complex project financials, resource tracking, or strict contractual reporting requirements (T&M, FFP, or cost-type contracts).
U.S. citizenship (required to hold and maintain the clearance level above).
Background in engineering, hardware/software systems, or solutions architecture, or a related field with hands-on experience running technical programs alongside engineering teams.

Preferred Qualifications

Familiarity with networking, telecom, or SDN/traffic engineering concepts.
Strong background in satellite and mission operations — early-orbit commissioning, fleet readiness, or operating in high-consequence environments.
Experience supporting programs that have transitioned from prototype to production volumes, and improving TRL/MRL along the way.
In-depth knowledge of USG acquisition processes, FAR/DFARS, and contract vehicles (BAAs, sole-source, IDIQs, OTAs).
Bachelor's degree in engineering, computer science, or a related technical field — preferred, not mandatory. Equivalent hands-on technical experience is evaluated on equal footing.
Willingness to travel occasionally as program needs require.

Compensation

The base salary for this role is $187,000 – $207,000, which may vary by geographic location. Compensation also includes a competitive equity grant, an annual performance bonus, and a comprehensive benefits package. Your final offer will reflect your location, skills, qualifications, and experience.

What We Offer

Innovative Environment: Work at a cutting-edge company shaping the future of aerospace communications.
Impactful Work: Directly contribute to critical national security programs and initiatives.
Growth Opportunities: Expand your career with opportunities for professional development and advancement.
Inclusive Culture: Be part of a collaborative, supportive, and inclusive workplace where your contributions matter.
Flexibility: Flexible working arrangements including hybrid remote/in-office schedules.
Compensation and Equity: Competitive salary, comprehensive benefits (401(k), dental, vision, health, life insurance), paid time off, and equity options.

ITAR/EAR Requirements

This position involves access to export-controlled information. To comply with U.S. government export regulations, applicants must meet one of the following criteria:

Qualify as a U.S. person, which includes:
U.S. citizen or national
U.S. lawful permanent resident (green card holder)
Refugee under 8 U.S.C. 1157
Asylee under 8 U.S.C. 1158
Be eligible to access export-controlled information without requiring an export authorization.
Be eligible and reasonably likely to obtain the necessary export authorization from the appropriate U.S. government agency.

The company reserves the right to decline pursuing an export licensing process for legitimate business-related reasons.

Equal Opportunity Employer Statement

Qualified applicants from all backgrounds are encouraged to apply.

new_jobs.title: GTM Data Analyst
new_jobs.description:
MarginEdge is hiring an Analyst
to build out go-to-market analytics: pipeline and conversion reporting, coverage and capacity modeling, commission calculation, and the analysis leadership uses to decide where to put money and headcount.

The enticing part of this role is that you own the whole path. You'll help frame the question, write the SQL, build the model, put it in source control, and present the answer — and the version you build is the one the company keeps using. There's no analytics team you hand a spec to. That's the trade: you have to be technical enough to build it, and you get to skip the six weeks of translation.

You'll report to the Director of Data Platform and Analytics and sit inside the data team, with Revenue Operations as your primary stakeholder. Your work gets reviewed by people who care whether the model is sound, and your roadmap comes from what the revenue organization actually needs. You'll work regularly with the Director of Revenue Operations, the CRO, and FP&A — more direct exposure to how revenue decisions get made than this kind of role usually carries.

We care much more about how you think and what you can build than where you've worked. Consulting, finance, RevOps, a BI seat at a smaller company, a science or engineering background you've since pointed at data problems — all fine.

MarginEdge: Where hospitality meets technology

As a team built by former (and current!) restaurant operators, our mission is to bring operators the same energy, attention to detail, and passion that they bring to their guests. Our culture is deeply rooted in service, partially because that’s where so many of our team come from (including everyone on our Business Development team), but also because we believe it is just the right way to run a business. We design our software with profound empathy for the complexity of running a restaurant, and the goal of making the magic just a little easier for operators by taking the complex (read: very annoying) back office tasks off their plate, while empowering them with real-time data.

Our founders share a deep history in both owning and operating restaurants and in building successful tech companies. We are venture-backed and serve 12,000+ restaurants across the US and Canada.

We enable restaurants to make magic while knowing we are doing the same for them.

We have the utmost respect for our clients and because of this, we are unable to hire their current employees.

What type of responsibilities will I have?

Build the analysis that decides things.

Build the analysis behind weekly pipeline reviews, forecast reviews, monthly business reviews, and sales board reporting, and take over more of it as you ramp.
Own stage-to-stage conversion reporting: conversion rates, cycle times, and win rates by channel, team, segment, and product.
Build assumption-based models for strategic initiatives — new segments, pricing changes, channel bets — with the assumptions parameterized rather than buried in a formula.
Help run and extend the coverage and capacity models: work the revenue target back to the pipeline and headcount required, and flag the gap early enough that leadership can act on it.
Contribute to the pipeline-based bottoms-up forecast and its reconciliation against the sales team commitment and the top-down model.
Investigate the unglamorous questions — why a cohort converted worse than the one before it, why cycle time moved in one segment and not another — and bring them to leadership before you're asked.

Build the thing that answers them next quarter.

Build and maintain the GTM layer of our dbt project: funnel and conversion models, pipeline history, rep and territory attribution.
Ship through source control — branch, pull request, review, tests, documentation. Your code gets reviewed, and eventually you'll review other people's.
Reconcile Salesforce, subscription billing, and product usage data, and become the person who can explain precisely why they disagree when they do.
Help define GTM metrics in our semantic layer, with RevOps as the metric owner, so self-service and agent-based querying return governed numbers rather than someone's best guess.

Use AI as a real tool and check its work.

Use Claude for query drafting, model scaffolding, and analysis iteration, and help RevOps stakeholders get useful work out of it.
QA AI output seriously: know what the query actually did, catch the plausible-but-wrong answer, and be able to explain the mechanism behind a finding rather than repeating it.

What qualifications or skills are required?

Demonstrated professional experience doing analytical work where you were expected to structure some of the problem yourself, not just execute a spec.
Strong SQL. CTEs, joins, and window functions should be comfortable. More importantly, when a query returns a number that looks wrong, you find out why rather than running it again.
Working knowledge of source control — branches, commits, pull requests. You don't need to have worked on a large codebase, but if your instinct is to build in a shared spreadsheet, this role will frustrate you.
Enough curiosity about how data gets where it is to reason about where a number came from and when it last landed. You won't own ingestion.
Real spreadsheet skill. A lot of what you produce lands in Excel in front of an executive, and you should be able to build a multi-tab model someone else can follow and extend.
The ability to say the number is wrong to a room that would prefer it weren't, and an obsession with accuracy that survives deadline pressure.
Funnel and SaaS metrics: conversion rate, pipeline coverage, cycle time, gross and net retention, CAC, payback. If you already know what breaks each one, great. If not, you'll learn them here, and you should be able to explain them by month three.

Nice To Haves

dbt — Core, project structure, tests, macros. If you've built tested, version-controlled transformation logic some other way, say so.
Trino/Athena or Snowflake. We're mid-migration, so you'd see both.
Python for the analysis SQL shouldn't do.
Salesforce as a data source, including the parts of it that lie to you.
Subscription billing data (Zuora or similar), quota setting, territory design, or sales compensation modeling.
Semantic or metrics layer experience (MetricFlow, Cube, or similar).
BI development in Preset/Superset, Looker, Tableau, or comparable.

Compensation:
The anticipated salary range for this role is $90,000–$110,000
annually. Where a candidate falls within that range depends on a variety of factors, including experience, skills, qualifications, geographic location, and internal equity. In addition to base salary, this role may be eligible for bonus opportunities and our comprehensive benefits package.

What’s it like to work for MarginEdge?

Imagine the fun of a great restaurant - surrounded by a team of people (including some that you help to manage!) who care about hospitality, care about quality, and care about each other - then subtract the long nights, weekends, drunk customers at the bar...et voila, MarginEdge!

We work hard, we work fast and we fuel our work with a commitment of transparency from leadership, straight talk and trust between teams. We believe that the best people do their best work when they feel empowered - so whether you are remote or in our office (likely eating a catered lunch from our clients in our baller, brand new penthouse HQ in Ballston) you get to work with your manager to call your shot on what works best for you. Did we mention it has a full commercial kitchen and is walking distance (covered walking, that is) from the metro?

Benefits (Shut The Front Door, They Are Amazing)

In order to fuel this rocket ship, we need to build a team as passionate about our work and product as we are. We believe that top talent (that’s you!) should feel deeply connected to their work, appreciated for the time they give to building our organization and have the balance necessary to give their best during work hours and all those after-hours too. We do this by offering a suite of kick ass benefits not only to be competitive and catch the eye of super smart people (that’s you again!) but also provide the foundation for a career you love and a life outside of work you love just as much.

Unlimited Paid Time Off (and we mean it, we encourage your healthy work life balance!)
Medical, Dental, Vision, and Short/Long-Term Disability Insurance (preventative care for the win)
Health Savings Account with employer match (dependent upon your medical plan selection)
Commuter benefits with employer contribution (excluding limos and helos - for now)
Generous Life Insurance Plan

Company-Paid Holidays
401(k) and matching
Stock Options to buy into everything we are doing to support this industry
12-week fully Paid Parental Leave
Lunch catered twice a week at our HQ in Arlington (we exclusively cater from our clients, too!
A wellness program that sponsors healthy activities such as step challenges and provides discounts to gyms and fitness classes.

Check out our 100% “Recommend to a Friend” rating from anonymous employee reviews on
Glassdoor
.

Oh, and our recognition in the Washington Post as a
top small businesses
to work for in 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025!

And most important, what our customers think about our work on
Capterra
and
G2 Crowd.

Our Fine Print is Bold:

We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran, marital, disability status or any other characteristic protected by law. You be you. While we are proudest of our commitment to exceptional culture and creating a truly excellent work environment, we see our benefits as an extension of that belief. Our benefits package is designed to be exceptionally competitive and a reflection of our commitment to a best-in-class workplace for all.

Our culture is deeply rooted in service—partially because that’s where we came from but also because we believe it's the right way to run a business. We design our software with profound empathy for the complexity of running a restaurant.

Our dream is to make the magic just a little easier for operators and their teams. We believe in crazy things like knowing how much waste your kitchen is producing and what your total spend is during the period. Solving these kinds of problems is really freaking hard to do, which is why we develop cutting-edge technology that answers these questions with data science.

.
Job Purpose

The CLIENTis seeking an experienced Information Security Program Manager to lead its ISO/IEC 27001:2022 program. The role holder will establish, maintain and continually improve CLIENT’s Information Security Management System (ISMS), manage information security and technical risk, and guide CLIENT through successful re-certification and surveillance audits, protecting the confidentiality, integrity and availability of information and systems that support Dubai’s healthcare services.
As a secondary responsibility, the role supports CLIENT’s IT Service Management System (ISO/IEC 20000-1) and Business Continuity Management System (ISO 22301), working towards an integrated management system approach.
Key Responsibilities

Plan, lead and manage the end-to-end ISO/IEC 27001 program, including ISMS scope definition, timelines, budget, resources and stakeholder reporting.
Review existing information security policies, standards, procedures and records to assess completeness and alignment with ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and ISO/IEC 27002.
Examine current security practices and controls across people, processes and technology to evaluate how effectively they operate in practice.
Conduct a detailed gap analysis against ISO/IEC 27001 requirements (Clauses 4–10 and Annex A controls) and produce a prioritized remediation roadmap.
Develop and maintain the information security risk management methodology, and conduct periodic technical risk assessments of applications, infrastructure, networks, cloud services and medical and clinical systems.
Maintain the information security risk register and risk treatment plans, and track the implementation of treatments with risk and control owners.
Coordinate periodic vulnerability assessments, penetration tests and configuration reviews, and ensure findings are risk-rated, remediated and verified.
Establish and manage a CIS-based compliance program, adopting the CIS Critical Security Controls (v8) and CIS Benchmarks as secure configuration baselines for operating systems, databases, network devices, cloud platforms and applications.
Conduct periodic CIS compliance assessments using automated scanning tools (e.g., CIS-CAT Pro, Tenable, Qualys), track compliance scores against agreed targets, and coordinate remediation or documented exceptions with system owners.
Prepare and maintain the Statement of Applicability (SoA) and the documentation required for the ISMS, including the ISMS scope, policy, objectives and supporting procedures.
Assess information security risks of third parties and suppliers, and ensure appropriate security requirements are included in contracts.
Establish and run the ISMS internal audit program and management reviews, and track nonconformities and corrective actions through to closure.
Prepare CLIENT for Stage 1 and Stage 2 re-certification audits and ongoing surveillance audits, coordinate with the certification body, and lead the response to any findings.
Define information security KPIs and metrics, and generate and present periodic (monthly and quarterly) reports covering risk posture, control effectiveness, vulnerability and remediation status, CIS compliance scores, security incidents, audit findings and awareness completion, to support management reviews and decision-making.
Drive information security awareness and training so that staff understand their responsibilities within the ISMS.
Ensure the ISMS aligns with CLIENT policies and applicable UAE and Dubai Government information security and data protection requirements, including the UAE Information Assurance Standards, Dubai Electronic Security Center (DESC) requirements and healthcare data regulations.

Secondary Responsibilities

Support the implementation, maintenance and certification of the IT Service Management System (ISO/IEC 20000-1) and the Business Continuity Management System (ISO 22301), working closely with the IT Service Management and Business Continuity teams.
Align ISMS controls with ITSM processes, including incident, problem, change, configuration, capacity, availability and supplier management.
Contribute to business impact analysis (BIA), the definition of recovery objectives (RTO/RPO) and continuity risk assessments for critical IT services and information assets.
Support the development, review and testing of IT service continuity, disaster recovery and business continuity plans, and ensure lessons learned are captured and acted upon.
Identify opportunities for an integrated management system across ISO/IEC 27001, ISO/IEC 20000-1 and ISO 22301, including shared policies, documentation, internal audits and management reviews.
Support internal and external audits for ISO/IEC 20000-1 and ISO 22301, including evidence preparation and follow-up of corrective actions.

Qualifications and Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Information Security, Information Technology, Computer Science or a related field.
[7–10]+ years of experience in information security, including at least [3] years leading ISMS, security risk or compliance programs.
Proven track record of leading at least one ISO/IEC 27001 implementation or certification.
In-depth knowledge of ISO/IEC 27001:2022, ISO/IEC 27002 and ISO/IEC 27005, and of risk assessment methodologies.
Hands-on experience implementing and assessing the CIS Critical Security Controls and CIS Benchmarks, including the use of configuration compliance scanning tools.
Solid technical understanding of networks, operating systems, cloud platforms, identity and access management, and security technologies (e.g., firewalls, SIEM, EDR, vulnerability scanners).
Working knowledge of ISO/IEC 20000-1 and ISO 22301; hands-on implementation or audit experience with these standards is a strong advantage.
Familiarity with UAE and Dubai information security regulations and healthcare data protection requirements.
Experience in healthcare or government environments is preferred.

Preferred Certifications

ISO/IEC 27001 Lead Implementer and/or Lead Auditor
CISSP, CISM or CISA
ISO/IEC 20000-1 and/or ISO 22301 Lead Implementer or Lead Auditor (advantageous)
CRISC or an equivalent risk management certification (advantageous)

Program and change management
Risk-based thinking and sound technical judgement
Stakeholder management and ability to influence without direct authority
Analytical thinking and attention to detail

Facilitation, coaching and training delivery

We are a small team operating inside a larger technology company, and we are growing quickly through our 2027 launch.

On a small team, that means organizing and managing projects for everyone at Center Stage, owning launches from plan to finish, and keeping priorities moving across product, marketing, partnerships, legal and operations. new_jobs.title: Senior Technical Program Manager, Engineering
new_jobs.description:
About Us

Sage Bionetworks uses open science and collaboration to improve human health. We bring together scientific, technical, and operational expertise to advance biomedical research through responsible data sharing, strong governance, and innovative approaches to research and technology. Our work is complex, interdisciplinary, and mission-driven. We value curiosity, diverse perspectives, experimentation, accountability, and radical collaboration.

The Opportunity

In this role you will be a member of the Technology Team, supporting both the Platform and Web Engineering teams whose work powers Synapse and the broader portfolio of Sage portals used by biomedical research communities worldwide. These teams serve many programs at once, from milestone-driven awards to long-running NIH-funded portals. You will apply your skills as a Technical Program Manager to enable Sage’s mission by bringing structure, discipline, and sustained stakeholder engagement to the delivery of our core data platform and web products.

Are you the type of person who enjoys engaging with software engineers, product leaders, scientific program managers, and the researchers who use our platforms every day? Do you have strong facilitation skills, and do you take satisfaction in driving prioritization decisions among stakeholders with competing needs? Do you want to build the operating foundation of a team’s program management practice from the ground up rather than inherit someone else’s processes? As Senior Technical Program Manager, you would bring your expertise and a passion for open science and collaboration to a role that is being established, not inherited, and whose day-to-day shape you will help define.

You’ll define and run the processes that turn stakeholder needs into committed work, maintain visibility into dependencies between the two teams, and coordinate across programs and portals so that execution aligns with Sage’s broader strategy. You'll also be the operational partner to Sage's product team and scientific program managers, translating product vision and funder commitments into reliably delivered work.

In this role, you will own the Platform and Web Engineering teams’ day-to-day operating discipline from day one, with structured mentorship and deliberately phased expansion into cross-portfolio and matrixed program leadership responsibilities as you grow in the role.

You'll Know You're Succeeding When

Stakeholders have a clear, consistent, and well-communicated process for surfacing issues and feature requests — and receive timely, substantive responses, including clear "no's" when warranted.
The Platform and Web Engineering teams operate on a predictable, coordinated delivery cadence that fits each team's working style, with well-maintained backlogs that reflect each team's work while making shared dependencies visible.
The workload overlap of Platform and Web Engineering for shared product initiatives is explicitly coordinated, not left to chance or to individual contributors to resolve.
Release dates are driven proactively, with risk surfaced early enough for stakeholders to adjust, and release communications arrive before the work lands in users' hands.
Cross-portal dependencies and known risks are surfaced early and tracked consistently, so product leadership can act on them before they become stakeholder-visible issues.
Prioritization decisions on the Platform and Web Engineering teams are informed by clear backlog data and consistent intake, giving leadership the inputs they need to make the harder trade-off calls.
Platform and product leadership can rely on you to translate strategy and roadmap into executed, shipped work.
Scientific program managers can rely on you as a dependable, communicative technical counterpart for program delivery and dependencies.
Stakeholders experience consistent, timely, and professional communication from the Platform and Web Engineering teams on the day-to-day work that affects them.
You are able to communicate with clarity and care when scope, timing, or feasibility require difficult conversations with funders or external partners.

Key Responsibilities

Program & Project Management

Intake & prioritization: Design and operate the Platform and Web Engineering teams' intake process for stakeholder requests, with clear pathways, triage criteria, and timely responses. Partner with product leadership to maintain a transparent prioritization framework across competing stakeholders.
Delivery planning & tracking: Build and maintain detailed delivery plans across concurrent initiatives; track feature-to-requirement mapping, commitments to funders and programs, and progress against committed dates.
Risk & escalation: Surface risks proactively, triage mitigations, and escalate honestly when scope, timeline, or resourcing is not viable as committed.
Metrics & reporting: Define and maintain the operational metrics that make the teams' work legible to stakeholders and leadership — throughput, predictability, issue aging, release cadence. Contribute to a monthly view of each team's capacity by program.
Proposal estimates: Provide realistic effort and cost estimates when new grants and contracts are written, so commitments match team capacity.

Delivery Cadence & Team Operations

Operating cadence facilitation: Run the teams' delivery ceremonies — planning sessions, standups, reviews, retrospectives, or equivalents — using the methodology that fits each team's working style. Bring Scrum, Kanban, and lightweight agile practices to the table as the situation calls for, without imposing a specific framework where it doesn't fit.
Backlog hygiene: Maintain clean, well-groomed backlogs for both teams, aligned with product priorities and team capacity, with shared dependencies clearly visible.
Release management: Drive hard release dates, coordinate deployment windows with program-side demos and user webinars, and partner with engineering on change management.
Platform and Web Engineering alignment: Act as the connection between the Platform and Web Engineering teams — maintaining visibility into shared workload, surfacing dependencies early, and ensuring both teams' delivery and release plans account for the other.
Process standards: Establish and iterate on the delivery methodology, documentation, and operating rhythms that fit the Platform and Web Engineering teams' work. Pay attention to what's working and adapt the practice to the teams rather than the reverse.

Stakeholder Engagement

Communication: Own cross-program communications about what is being deployed, when, what the expected impact is, and what stakeholders need to do to be ready — including surfacing when a change delivered for one program has implications or adoption opportunities for others.
Relationship-building: Build and maintain effective working relationships with a wide spectrum of stakeholders — program leads, portal owners, scientific program managers, external partners, and funders — tailoring your approach to the needs and context of each stakeholder group.
Negotiation: Lead honest, collaborative negotiations with internal and external stakeholders on scope, timing, and trade-offs. Surface constraints early, offer alternatives where possible, and ensure difficult conversations (“no,” “not yet,” “not as scoped”) are communicated clearly and in time for stakeholders to plan accordingly.
External representation: Act as a credible, prepared technical representative with external partners and funders. Partner with internal leadership to determine when escalation is warranted, and step in front of funders directly when navigating a delayed deliverable, a de-scoped feature, or a shift in what is realistic to commit to.

Cross-Portfolio Support

Cross-portfolio visibility: Contribute to a cross-portal view of features, bugs, and dependencies by keeping the Platform and Web Engineering teams' data clean and up to date. Flag emerging risks, dependencies, and leverage opportunities to your supervisor and product leadership.
Cross-functional coordination: Collaborate with program managers on other engineering teams and across the Science & Data team (SciData), and with the IT and Cybersecurity lead on security and compliance work, to surface dependencies affecting the Platform and Web Engineering teams’ work.

AI-Enabled Program Operations

Design AI-assisted and agentic workflows for intake, status reporting, risk tracking and estimation. Refine workflows and adopt AI-enabled tools to reduce friction, increase throughput, and improve the predictability and quality of program operations.

Qualifications

Education

Bachelor’s degree

Experience

5+ years of experience in program or project management for software, data platform, or technology teams.
Demonstrated experience running a delivery practice end-to-end — intake, backlog refinement, delivery ceremonies, release management, retrospectives — including fluency with Scrum, Kanban, or other agile methodologies and the judgment to apply what fits a team rather than impose a specific framework.
Experience running program/project management for multiple engineering teams that share workload or dependencies, or demonstrated ability to coordinate across teams with closely related scope.
Experience building effective working relationships with technical and non-technical stakeholders, with a thoughtful, professional approach to engaging stakeholders.
Experience coordinating delivery across multiple concurrent initiatives, programs, or funders with competing priorities.
Strong facilitation skills, including the ability to drive prioritization decisions among competing stakeholders and to communicate difficult trade-offs clearly.
Comfort working closely with software engineers on release coordination, deployment planning, and change management.
Strong written and verbal communication skills; ability to translate between technical execution and program and business context.
Ability to hold a predictable operating cadence under real-world pressure, in environments where resources are constrained and priorities shift.

Nice to have

Here at Siemens, we take pride in enabling sustainable progress through technology. We do this through empowering customers by combining the real and digital worlds. We are building intelligent systems that bring generative AI into the physical world - merging models, embodiment, and real-time perception into entirely new product experiences. As a Data Program Manager are responsible for all aspects of data acquisition for the next generation of AI products by working on cross-functional DAI (data and artificial intelligence) data programs that support Siemens’ AI and industrial AI initiatives. Here you will partner with applied science, product, engineering, and operations to design and implement pragmatic solutions for acquiring data. You will be a key interface between our product roadmap and external data offerings.

The role will own multiple related workstreams and serve as a liaison across Product, Engineering, Applied Science, Legal, Compliance, Procurement, and external data partners. The Data Program Manager will translate business and product needs into executable data programs, establish operating mechanisms, manage dependencies and risks, and drive programs through delivery.

Manage complex, cross-functional AI data programs and interconnected workstreams from planning through delivery, aligning evolving requirements with clear objectives, milestones, and operating plans.
Drive execution across Product, Engineering, Applied Science, Legal, Compliance, Procurement, Security, and other stakeholders, while representing programs in leadership forums.
Oversee end-to-end data acquisition, annotation, curation, licensing, and readiness, and manage strategic day-to-day relationships with internal and external data owners
Establish success metrics, requirements, and acceptance criteria for data deliverables to measure progress, quality, readiness, and compliance with organizational policies.
Identify systemic risks, resolve complex cross-organizational dependencies, and lead regular program reviews to communicate status and decisions to senior leadership.
Manage budgets, resource planning, and vendor commitments while developing scalable governance models, templates, and operating processes to improve program efficiency.

Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience.
6+ years of experience in program management, project management, operations, technology programs, data programs, or a related field.
Demonstrated experience independently leading complex, cross-functional programs.
Experience managing multiple workstreams, dependencies, stakeholders, and external partners.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including communication with senior stakeholders.
Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience managing AI, data, software, or technology programs.
Experience with data acquisition, data annotation, data curation, or data lifecycle programs.
Experience developing and executing data acquisition strategies that leverage frontier AI models for data discovery, generation, enrichment, transformation, and quality evaluation, with an understanding of when to apply AI-driven approaches versus traditional or human-in-the-loop methods.
Familiarity with data governance, data privacy, licensing, or responsible AI principles.
Experience managing strategic vendors or external data providers.
Experience establishing program governance, operating mechanisms, or standardized processes.
